lpp.card_rebate_program.rebate_bps_at_ta.description: Rebate rate in basis points awarded when the card program's spend target is achieved.

lpp.card_settlement_line.cross_border.name: cross_border
lpp.card_settlement_line.cross_border.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the card transaction crossed international borders (i.e., the issuer country differs from the merchant country).

lpp.card_settlement_line.gross_amount.name: gross_amount
lpp.card_settlement_line.gross_amount.description: Total gross settlement amount for the card transaction line before any fees or deductions.
lpp.card_settlement_line.gross_amount.value_scale: Currency units (likely USD), stored in full dollars/cents as a decimal

lpp.card_settlement_line.interchange_bps.name: interchange_bps
lpp.card_settlement_line.interchange_bps.description: Interchange fee rate for the card transaction expressed in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%).

lpp.card_settlement_line.issuer_country.name: issuer_country
lpp.card_settlement_line.issuer_country.description: ISO 2-letter country code identifying the country of the card-issuing bank.

lpp.cash_balance.amount.name: amount
lpp.cash_balance.amount.description: The cash balance amount for the given date and currency.

lpp.cash_balance.balance_date.name: balance_date
lpp.cash_balance.balance_date.description: The calendar date as of which the cash balance is recorded.

lpp.cash_balance.currency_code.name: currency_code
lpp.cash_balance.currency_code.description: ISO 3-letter currency code identifying the denomination of the cash balance (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP).

lpp.cash_flow.flow_amount.name: flow_amount
lpp.cash_flow.flow_amount.description: Monetary value of the cash flow transaction.
lpp.cash_flow.flow_amount.value_scale: Monetary amount in the currency specified by flow_currency, stored in full units

lpp.cash_flow.flow_currency.name: flow_currency
lpp.cash_flow.flow_currency.description: ISO 4217 3-letter currency code of the cash flow transaction (e.g. EUR, USD, GBP).

lpp.cash_flow.reference.name: reference
lpp.cash_flow.reference.description: Free-text reference identifier associated with the cash flow transaction.

lpp.cash_flow.status.name: status
lpp.cash_flow.status.description: Confirmation status of the cash flow, indicating whether it is an actuals-backed confirmed entry or a forward-looking forecast.

lpp.cash_flow.transaction_date.name: transaction_date
lpp.cash_flow.transaction_date.description: Calendar date on which the cash flow transaction was initiated or recorded.

lpp.cash_flow.value_date.name: value_date
lpp.cash_flow.value_date.description: Calendar date on which the cash flow is expected to settle and funds become effective.

lpp.chargeback.amount.name: amount
lpp.chargeback.amount.description: Monetary value of the chargeback dispute filed against a transaction.
lpp.chargeback.amount.value_scale: Currency amount, assumed USD stored in full dollars

lpp.chargeback.classification.name: classification
lpp.chargeback.classification.description: Category classification of the chargeback, indicating the type or nature of the dispute (e.g., fraud, consumer dispute, processing error).

lpp.chargeback.initiated_date.name: initiated_date
lpp.chargeback.initiated_date.description: Calendar date on which the chargeback was initiated or filed.

lpp.chargeback.reason_category.name: reason_category
lpp.chargeback.reason_category.description: High-level grouping of the reason for the chargeback (e.g., fraud, authorization, processing error, consumer dispute).

lpp.chargeback.reason_code.name: reason_code
lpp.chargeback.reason_code.description: Standardized card network reason code identifying the specific grounds for the chargeback (e.g., Visa or Mastercard reason codes).

lpp.chargeback.resolved_date.name: resolved_date
lpp.chargeback.resolved_date.description: Calendar date on which the chargeback case was resolved or closed.

lpp.chargeback.status.name: status
lpp.chargeback.status.description: Current processing status of the chargeback case (e.g., open, pending, won, lost, closed).

lpp.company.code.name: code
lpp.company.code.description: Internal company code identifier, typically structured as a regional prefix followed by a country or entity suffix (e.g. 'GR_AE', 'GR_AU').

lpp.company.country.name: country
lpp.company.country.description: Country associated with the company, likely an ISO 2-letter country code or full country name.

lpp.company.lei.name: lei
lpp.company.lei.description: Legal Entity Identifier (LEI), a 20-character alphanumeric code used globally to uniquely identify a legal entity.

lpp.company.name.name: name
lpp.company.name.description: The legal or registered name of the company.

lpp.company_financial_metric.debt_to_ebi.name: debt_to_ebitda
lpp.company_financial_metric.debt_to_ebi.description: Ratio of total debt divided by EBITDA, a leverage metric indicating how many years of earnings would be needed to repay debt.
lpp.company_financial_metric.debt_to_ebi.value_scale: Ratio expressed as a multiple (e.g., 3.5x means debt is 3.5 times EBITDA)

lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_eps.name: diluted_eps
lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_eps.description: Diluted earnings per share, representing net income attributable to each diluted share including options, warrants, and convertible securities.
lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_eps.value_scale: USD per share, stored in full dollars

lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_sha.name: diluted_shares_outstanding
lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_sha.description: Total number of diluted shares outstanding, including common shares plus the dilutive effect of options, warrants, and convertible instruments.
lpp.company_financial_metric.diluted_sha.value_scale: Number of shares, stored as actual count (not in thousands or millions)

lpp.company_financial_metric.ebitda.name: ebitda
lpp.company_financial_metric.ebitda.description: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, a proxy for operating cash profitability.

lpp.company_financial_metric.free_cash_f.name: free_cash_flow
lpp.company_financial_metric.free_cash_f.description: Free cash flow representing operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, indicating cash available after maintaining or expanding assets.

lpp.company_financial_metric.net_debt.name: net_debt
lpp.company_financial_metric.net_debt.description: Net debt calculated as total debt minus cash and cash equivalents, representing a company's net financial obligation.

lpp.company_financial_metric.period_date.name: period_date
lpp.company_financial_metric.period_date.description: The calendar date marking the end of the reporting period (e.g., 2023-12-31 for full-year, 2023-09-30 for Q3).

lpp.company_financial_metric.period_type.name: period_type
lpp.company_financial_metric.period_type.description: Code indicating the type of financial reporting period: Q (quarterly), FY (full fiscal year), or TTM (trailing twelve months).

lpp.company_financial_metric.revenue.name: revenue
lpp.company_financial_metric.revenue.description: Total revenue (top-line sales) recognized by the company during the reporting period.

lpp.company_financial_metric.wacc_pct.name: wacc_pct
lpp.company_financial_metric.wacc_pct.description: Weighted average cost of capital expressed as a percentage, representing the blended required rate of return across all capital sources.

lpp.counterparty_exposure.as_of_date.name: as_of_date
lpp.counterparty_exposure.as_of_date.description: The reporting date as of which the counterparty exposure snapshot was taken.

lpp.counterparty_exposure.reporting_curr.name: reporting_currency
lpp.counterparty_exposure.reporting_curr.description: ISO 3-letter currency code in which exposure amounts are reported (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP).

lpp.counterparty_exposure.total_exposure.name: total_exposure
lpp.counterparty_exposure.total_exposure.description: Total aggregated counterparty exposure expressed in the reporting currency.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.total_exposure.value_scale: Reporting currency units, stored at full value (no scaling)

lpp.credit_rating.agency.name: agency
lpp.credit_rating.agency.description: Credit rating agency that issued the rating (e.g. Moody's, S&P, Fitch).

lpp.credit_rating.as_of_date.name: as_of_date
lpp.credit_rating.as_of_date.description: The effective date on which the credit rating was assigned or last updated.

lpp.credit_rating.is_current.name: is_current
lpp.credit_rating.is_current.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this rating record is the most current active rating for the entity.

lpp.credit_rating.outlook.name: outlook
lpp.credit_rating.outlook.description: Credit rating agency's directional outlook on the rated entity's future rating trajectory (e.g. STABLE, POSITIVE).

lpp.credit_rating.rating_grade.name: rating_grade
lpp.credit_rating.rating_grade.description: Alphanumeric credit rating symbol assigned by the agency reflecting the entity's creditworthiness (e.g. A1, A+, AA-, BBB+).

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.corridor.name: corridor
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.corridor.description: Payment corridor representing the origin-to-destination regional route of a cross-border transaction (e.g. 'US-EU', 'EU-APAC').

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.destination.name: destination_country
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.destination.description: ISO 2-letter country code of the payment destination country.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.fx_spread_b.name: fx_spread_bps
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.fx_spread_b.description: Foreign exchange spread charged on the payment leg, expressed in basis points.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.lifting_fee.name: lifting_fees
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.lifting_fee.description: Fees charged for processing and lifting a cross-border payment leg, stored as a numeric amount.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.origination.name: origination_country
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.origination.description: ISO 2-letter country code of the country where the cross-border payment originates.

lpp.currency.code.name: code
lpp.currency.code.description: ISO 4217 3-letter currency code (e.g. AED, AUD, BRL).

lpp.currency.description.name: description
lpp.currency.description.description: Full human-readable name of the currency (e.g. Australian Dollar, Swiss Franc).

lpp.third_party.code.name: code
lpp.third_party.code.description: Unique alphanumeric code identifying a third-party entity (e.g. 'RETAIL_CONSUMER', 'TP_CUST_0001').

lpp.third_party.name.name: name
lpp.third_party.name.description: Full display name of the third-party entity, such as a retail partner or aggregated consumer group (e.g. 'Macys Partner 1', 'Aggregated Retail Consumer').

lpp.derivative_mtm.mtm_amount.name: mtm_amount
lpp.derivative_mtm.mtm_amount.description: Mark-to-market (MTM) monetary value of a derivative position as of the valuation date.
lpp.derivative_mtm.mtm_amount.value_scale: Monetary amount in the currency specified by mtm_currency, stored at full unit scale

lpp.derivative_mtm.mtm_currency.name: mtm_currency
lpp.derivative_mtm.mtm_currency.description: ISO 3-letter currency code in which the mark-to-market amount is denominated.

lpp.derivative_mtm.valuation_date.name: valuation_date
lpp.derivative_mtm.valuation_date.description: The date on which the derivative mark-to-market valuation was performed.

lpp.equity_action.action_date.name: action_date
lpp.equity_action.action_date.description: The calendar date on which the equity corporate action (e.g. dividend payment, buyback) took place.

lpp.equity_action.action_type.name: action_type
lpp.equity_action.action_type.description: Category of equity corporate action taken, such as BUYBACK, DIVIDEND, or SPECIAL_DIVIDEND.

lpp.equity_action.dividend_per_share.name: dividend_per_share
lpp.equity_action.dividend_per_share.description: The monetary dividend amount paid out per individual share for dividend-type actions.
lpp.equity_action.dividend_per_share.value_scale: Currency units per share; assumed USD unless otherwise specified

lpp.equity_action.price_per_share.name: price_per_share
lpp.equity_action.price_per_share.description: The price per share at which the equity action (e.g. buyback) was executed.
lpp.equity_action.price_per_share.value_scale: Currency units per share; assumed USD unless otherwise specified

lpp.equity_action.shares.name: shares
lpp.equity_action.shares.description: The number of shares involved in the equity action (e.g. shares repurchased or shares receiving a dividend).
lpp.equity_action.shares.value_scale: Count of shares, stored as whole or fractional shares

lpp.equity_action.total_amount.name: total_amount
lpp.equity_action.total_amount.description: The total monetary value of the equity action, calculated as shares multiplied by the relevant per-share price or dividend.
lpp.equity_action.total_amount.value_scale: Currency units (assumed USD), stored as full monetary value

lpp.fee_rate_card.currency_code.name: currency_code
lpp.fee_rate_card.currency_code.description: ISO 4217 3-letter currency code identifying the currency applicable to the fee rate card entry.

lpp.fee_rate_card.negotiated_rate.name: negotiated_rate
lpp.fee_rate_card.negotiated_rate.description: The contractually agreed fee rate applied to a transaction or service, as defined in the rate card.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.currency_code.name: currency_code
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.currency_code.description: ISO 4217 3-letter currency code indicating the currency of the cash flow (e.g. USD, GBP, JPY).

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.name: flow_category
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.description: Business classification of the cash flow type, such as capital expenditure, tax payments, accounts receivable collections, intercompany transfers, debt service, or accounts payable disbursements.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.forecast_date.name: forecast_date
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.forecast_date.description: The projected calendar date (month-start) for which the cash flow amount is forecasted.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.forecast_amount.name: forecast_amount
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.forecast_amount.description: The forecasted monetary value of the cash flow for the given category, currency, and date.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.forecast_amount.value_scale: Stored in full currency units, denominated in the currency specified by currency_code

lpp.forecast_snapshot.description.name: description

lpp.forecast_snapshot.snapshot_date.name: snapshot_date
lpp.forecast_snapshot.snapshot_date.description: The calendar date on which the forecast snapshot was captured or published.

lpp.forecast_snapshot.snapshot_id.name: snapshot_id
lpp.forecast_snapshot.snapshot_id.description: Unique identifier for a forecast snapshot, encoded as a combination of a prefix, date, and frequency code (e.g. 'FC_20230801_M').

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.actual_amount.name: actual_amount
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.actual_amount.description: The realized/actual monetary amount recorded for the cash flow category in the given period.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.actual_amount.value_scale: Monetary amount in the currency indicated by currency_code, stored in full units

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.currency_code.name: currency_code
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.currency_code.description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code denoting the currency in which amounts are denominated.

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.flow_category.name: flow_category
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.flow_category.description: Business classification of the cash flow type, such as PAYROLL, CAPEX, AP_DISBURSEMENT, AR_COLLECTION, TAX, or FX_REVAL.

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.forecast_amount.name: forecast_amount
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.forecast_amount.description: The budgeted or forecasted monetary amount projected for the cash flow category in the given period.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.forecast_amount.value_scale: Monetary amount in the currency indicated by currency_code, stored in full units

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.period_date.name: period_date
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.period_date.description: Month-end date representing the reporting period for the forecast vs. actual comparison.

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.variance_amount.name: variance_amount
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.variance_amount.description: The absolute monetary difference between the actual and forecast amounts for the cash flow category in the given period.

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.variance_pct.name: variance_pct
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.variance_pct.description: Percentage variance between actual and forecast amounts, stored on a whole-number percentage scale (e.g., -1.0000 = -1%).

lpp.fraud_detection_event.decision.name: decision
lpp.fraud_detection_event.decision.description: Fraud detection outcome for a transaction event, indicating whether it was allowed, flagged for review, or blocked.

lpp.fraud_loss.auth_method.name: auth_method
lpp.fraud_loss.auth_method.description: Authentication method used during the transaction, such as 3D Secure challenged, frictionless, or no 3DS.

lpp.fraud_loss.channel.name: channel
lpp.fraud_loss.channel.description: Sales or transaction channel through which the fraud loss occurred, such as in-warehouse, ecommerce, or membership renewal.

lpp.fraud_loss.fraud_vector.description: The method or attack vector by which the fraud was perpetrated, either social engineering or card-not-present.

lpp.fraud_loss.loss_amount.name: loss_amount
lpp.fraud_loss.loss_amount.description: Monetary value of the fraud loss recorded for the transaction.

lpp.fraud_loss.loss_category.name: loss_category
lpp.fraud_loss.loss_category.description: Classification of the fraud loss as either true fraud (unauthorized) or friendly fraud (disputed legitimate transaction).

lpp.fraud_loss.loss_date.name: loss_date
lpp.fraud_loss.loss_date.description: Calendar date on which the fraud loss was recorded or occurred.

lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.direction.name: direction

lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.tenor_bucket.name: tenor_bucket
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.tenor_bucket.description: Time-to-maturity bucket classifying the FX exposure into short-dated ranges (e.g. 0–1 month, 1–3 months, 3–6 months).

lpp.fx_forward.deal_id.name: deal_id
lpp.fx_forward.deal_id.description: Unique alphanumeric identifier for an FX forward deal (e.g. FXF-0001164).

lpp.fx_forward.status.name: status
lpp.fx_forward.status.description: Current lifecycle status of the FX forward deal: OPEN, SETTLED, or CANCELLED.

lpp.fx_forward.trade_date.name: trade_date
lpp.fx_forward.trade_date.description: The calendar date on which the FX forward deal was executed or booked.

lpp.fx_forward.value_date.name: value_date
lpp.fx_forward.value_date.description: The settlement date on which the currency exchange of the FX forward is due to occur.

lpp.fx_rate.rate.name: rate
lpp.fx_rate.rate.description: The foreign exchange conversion rate between two currencies for a given date and rate type.

lpp.fx_rate.rate_date.name: rate_date
lpp.fx_rate.rate_date.description: The calendar date on which the foreign exchange rate is effective.

lpp.fx_rate.rate_type.name: rate_type
lpp.fx_rate.rate_type.description: The classification of the FX rate, indicating whether it is a closing, spot, or average rate (e.g. 'CLOSING', 'SPOT', 'AVG').

lpp.gl_balance.amount.name: amount
lpp.gl_balance.amount.description: Monetary balance amount recorded for the GL account in the given currency and period.

lpp.gl_balance.balance_date.name: balance_date
lpp.gl_balance.balance_date.description: Month-end date for which the GL balance is recorded (e.g. 2023-06-30, 2024-02-29).

lpp.gl_balance.gl_account_ref.description: Primary key reference code identifying the General Ledger account to which the balance belongs.

lpp.gl_reconciliation.as_of_date.name: as_of_date
lpp.gl_reconciliation.as_of_date.description: Month-end date as of which the GL reconciliation snapshot was taken (e.g. 2025-03-31, 2024-02-29).

lpp.hedge_relationship.code.name: code

lpp.investment_position.as_of_date.description: The snapshot/valuation date as of which the investment position is recorded.

lpp.ach_return.description: Represents ACH (Automated Clearing House) payment transactions that were returned by the receiving bank, capturing the reason and amount for each return event. Each row records a single returned ACH transaction, identified by its return date, NACHA reason code, and return category. Key attributes include the monetary amount, standardized return reason codes (e.g. R01–R10), and high-level return categories such as INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, INVALID_ACCT, and UNAUTHORIZED.
lpp.ach_return.table_type_reason: Records discrete payment return events with a monetary amount, a date, and reason codes — classic fact table pattern despite low row count.
lpp.ach_return.grain: One row per returned ACH transaction, identified by its return date and reason code.

lpp.acquirer.description: A reference lookup table of acquiring banks and payment processors used by the organization to settle card transactions. Each row represents a single acquirer entity, identified by an internal code (e.g. ADYEN, STRIPE) and its full legal name. Key attributes include the acquirer's short code, full trading name, and the geographic region (AMER, EMEA) in which it operates.
lpp.acquirer.grain: One row per acquiring bank or payment processor.

lpp.acquirer_contract.description: Stores the contractual terms agreed between the organization and each acquiring bank or payment processor, including pricing, settlement timing, and service levels. Each row represents a single contract with a specific acquirer, covering an effective date range and lifecycle status. Key attributes include processor margin in basis points, settlement lag in business days, uptime SLA percentage, and contract effective/expiry dates.
lpp.acquirer_contract.table_type_reason: Describes slowly changing contractual attributes of acquirer relationships rather than being a static code lookup — better classified as a dimension.
lpp.acquirer_contract.grain: One row per acquirer contract, covering a specific effective date range.

lpp.acquirer_sla_metric.description: Tracks daily operational performance metrics for each acquirer against their contracted service level agreements, including authorization rates, settlement timeliness, and system uptime. Each row captures the measured SLA performance of a single acquirer on a specific calendar date. Key identifiers are the acquirer reference and the measurement date, with measures including auth_rate_pct, settlement_on_time_pct, and uptime_pct.
lpp.acquirer_sla_metric.grain: One row per acquirer per measurement date, recording that acquirer's SLA performance metrics for that day.

lpp.ap_invoice.description: Represents accounts payable invoices received from suppliers, tracking the full lifecycle from issuance through payment across multiple currencies and payment terms. Each row corresponds to a single supplier invoice, uniquely identified by its invoice number (e.g. AP-00090794). Key attributes include invoice amount, issue date, due date, paid date, payment terms (e.g. NET_30, NET_90), current status (PAID, OPEN, DISPUTED, PARTIAL), and summary metrics such as total billed, total paid, and on-time payment rate.
lpp.ap_invoice.table_type_reason: Contains transactional monetary measures (invoice_amount, total_billed, total_paid), lifecycle dates, and status tracking for individual invoice events — characteristic of a fact table rather than a pure dimension.
lpp.ap_invoice.grain: One row per accounts payable invoice, identified by a unique invoice number.

lpp.ar_invoice.description: Represents accounts receivable invoices issued to customers, capturing the full lifecycle of each billing event from issuance through payment or write-off. One row corresponds to a single invoice identified by a unique invoice_number that encodes channel, region, and date. Key attributes include invoice_amount, currency_code, issue_date, due_date, paid_date, payment_terms, and lifecycle status (OPEN, PAID, WRITTEN_OFF).
lpp.ar_invoice.table_type_reason: Contains measurable financial amounts (invoice_amount), lifecycle dates, and status — characteristics of a fact/event record rather than a descriptive dimension.
lpp.ar_invoice.grain: One row per accounts receivable invoice issued to a customer.

lpp.bank_statement_balance.description: Captures daily balance snapshots from bank statements across multiple accounts and currencies, representing the monetary position of a bank account on a given statement date. Each row records the balance amount, its currency, and a data quality validation outcome for that snapshot. Key identifiers are account_ref (distribution key) and statement_date (sort key and primary key).
lpp.bank_statement_balance.table_type_reason: Represents periodic balance snapshots with a numeric measure (amount) keyed by account and date — a periodic snapshot fact pattern, not a dimension.
lpp.bank_statement_balance.grain: One row per bank account per statement date balance snapshot.

lpp.bank.description: A reference dimension table containing master data for each banking institution the company works with. Each row represents a single bank identified by an internal code, with additional standard identifiers including SWIFT/BIC code and LEI for regulatory and cross-system matching. Key attributes include the internal code, display name (description1), BIC, and LEI.
lpp.bank.table_type_reason: Very small row count (14 rows), distributed ALL, contains only descriptive/identifier attributes — a classic reference/lookup table for banking institutions.

lpp.bank_account.description: A dimension table holding master data and rolled-up cash metrics for each corporate bank account, structured by region, country, and account purpose. Each row represents a single bank account (or logical account grouping) as of a rollup date, with the account's currency, total cash balance, and count of underlying sub-accounts. The internal code (e.g. GR_AE_COLLECTION_1) serves as the primary identifier.
lpp.bank_account.grain: One row per bank account (or account rollup group) per rollup date.

lpp.bank_account_signatory.description: Tracks authorized signatories assigned to corporate bank accounts, recording each individual's role, authority limit, current authorization status, and the date their authorization must be recertified. One row represents a single signatory-to-bank-account authorization relationship. Key attributes include authority_limit_amount, role, status, and next_recertify_due_date.
lpp.bank_account_signatory.table_type_reason: Small row count (440), distributed ALL, represents a governance/authorization reference relationship rather than a transactional fact or analytical dimension.
lpp.bank_account_signatory.grain: One row per signatory authorization on a bank account.

lpp.bank_branch.description: This table is a reference catalogue of bank branches used across the organisation, encoding each branch's bank affiliation and physical location. One row represents a single bank branch, identified by a structured code (e.g. 'BR_ANZ_SYD') that encodes the bank and city. Key identifiers include the branch code, ISO country code, and high-level geographic region (APAC, AMER, LATAM, EMEA, MENA).

lpp.bank_fee.description: This table records individual bank fee charges levied against the organisation by its banking partners, capturing the date, amount, and currency of each fee. One row represents a single bank fee charge event on a given date. Key attributes include the charge date, charged amount, currency code, and a flag indicating whether the fee has been raised for review.
lpp.bank_fee.table_type_reason: Contains transactional fee charge events with monetary amounts and dates, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.bank_fee.grain: One row per bank fee charge event.

lpp.bank_service_type.description: This table is a reference lookup of standardised bank service type codes and their human-readable descriptions, covering services such as account maintenance, wire transfers, and ACH credits. One row represents a single bank service type classification. The primary key is the numeric-string service code (e.g. '100', '250'), paired with a descriptive label.
lpp.bank_service_type.grain: One row per bank service type code.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.description: This table stores curated institutional or tribal knowledge facts — rules, assumptions, and guidelines — that inform business processes and analytical models within the organisation. One row represents a single knowledge fact with a defined validity window, confidence rating, and trigger condition. Key attributes include the fact type, narrative, title, effective dates, and lifecycle status.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_fact.grain: One row per tribal knowledge fact.

lpp.benchmark_rate.description: This table stores daily published values for major interest rate benchmarks (e.g. SOFR, ESTR, SONIA, TONA) across currencies and tenors, serving as the authoritative rate reference for pricing, hedging, and debt calculations. One row represents the published rate for a specific benchmark code, tenor, and date combination. Key identifiers are the composite of benchmark_code, rate_date, and tenor, with the associated currency_code and rate value.
lpp.benchmark_rate.grain: One row per benchmark code, tenor, and rate date combination.

lpp.credit_facility.description: Represents a corporate credit facility agreement, capturing the contractual terms under which a borrower may draw funds. Each row describes a single facility with its committed limit, tenor, floating rate benchmark, credit spread, and lifecycle status. Key identifiers include the facility code (e.g. CF_RCF_USD_2B) and benchmark_code (e.g. SOFR, ESTR, SONIA).
lpp.credit_facility.table_type_reason: With only 17 rows and serving as a reference/master record for borrowing facilities, this is a slowly-changing dimension describing credit facility entities rather than a generic reference table.
lpp.credit_facility.grain: One row per credit facility agreement.

lpp.borrowing.description: Records individual drawdown events against credit facilities, capturing the principal amount borrowed, the all-in interest rate, currency, drawdown date, repayment date, and current repayment status. Each row represents a single loan drawdown or tranche, linked to its parent facility via facility_ref. Status values (REPAID / OUTSTANDING) allow tracking of the live debt book.
lpp.borrowing.table_type_reason: Each row records a discrete borrowing/drawdown event with a principal amount and rate — this is a transactional fact rather than a dimension.
lpp.borrowing.grain: One row per individual loan drawdown or borrowing tranche.

lpp.brain_evaluation.description: Stores evaluation records generated by the AI 'brain' system when processing natural-language queries, capturing the query text, the produced answer summary, the timestamp of evaluation, and the number of graph expansion hops used. Each row represents a single query-evaluation run submitted to the brain system. This table is currently empty (row_count = 0) and likely used for logging and quality assessment of AI-generated answers.
lpp.brain_evaluation.table_type_reason: This is a logging/evaluation capture table for an AI query system with zero rows; it functions as a staging or operational log rather than a true reference or analytical table.
lpp.brain_evaluation.grain: One row per brain evaluation query run.

lpp.capital_allocation_actual.description: Tracks the actual capital deployed across strategic allocation buckets (CAPEX, M&A, Dividends, Debt Paydown, Buybacks) on a quarterly basis, alongside the framework target percentage for each bucket. Each row represents the actual allocation amount and target ratio for a specific capital bucket in a given quarter-end reporting period. Key identifiers are the composite of period_date and bucket.
lpp.capital_allocation_actual.table_type_reason: Rows capture periodic measured amounts (actuals vs. targets) per bucket and period — this is a periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.capital_allocation_actual.grain: One row per capital allocation bucket per quarter-end reporting period.

lpp.card_authorization.description: Captures individual card authorization request and response events processed through the acquiring network, including the authorization outcome (APPROVED, DECLINED, TIMEOUT, ERROR), transaction amount, currency, 3DS authentication status, card-not-present indicator, and response latency. Each row represents a single card authorization attempt identified by its acquirer reference and request timestamp. Key identifiers are acquirer_ref and auth_request_ts.
lpp.card_authorization.table_type_reason: Each row is a discrete authorization event with measurable amounts, timestamps, and outcomes — a classic transactional fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.card_authorization.grain: One row per card authorization request attempt.

lpp.card_settlement_batch.description: Represents a rolled-up summary of card payment transactions grouped into a settlement batch submitted by a payment processor to a merchant. Each row captures the financial outcome of a single batch, including gross sales, interchange fees, network assessment fees, processor margin, and net settlement amount. Key identifiers include acquirer_ref (distribution key), batch_close_ts (sort key), and processor_settle_ts.
lpp.card_settlement_batch.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive financial measures (gross_sales, interchange, net_settlement, network_assess, processor_margin) aggregated per settlement batch event, making it clearly a fact table despite the low inferred confidence of 0.47.
lpp.card_settlement_batch.grain: One row per card settlement batch closed by a payment processor for a merchant.

lpp.card_network.description: A reference lookup table representing card payment networks supported by the system. Each row describes a distinct card network with its short code, full display name, and payment type classification. Key identifiers include the primary key code (e.g., VISA, MASTERCARD, AMEX, UNIONPAY).
lpp.card_network.grain: One row per card network (e.g., Visa, Mastercard, American Express).

lpp.card_rebate_earning.description: Tracks the rebate amounts earned by the organization under corporate card rebate programs for each reporting period. Each row captures the eligible spend, rebate earned, and spend category for a specific period end date, enabling monitoring of rebate income against card program targets. Key identifiers include program_ref (distribution key) and period_date (sort key).
lpp.card_rebate_earning.table_type_reason: Contains additive financial measures (eligible_spend, rebate_earned) recorded at the grain of program/period/spend-category, which is characteristic of a periodic snapshot fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.card_rebate_earning.grain: One row per card rebate program, spend category, and reporting period end date.

lpp.card_rebate_program.description: A reference table defining the corporate card rebate programs available to the organization, typically negotiated with banks or card issuers. Each row describes a single program including its unique code, program type (e.g., virtual card, commercial card, purchasing card), and the rebate rate in basis points awarded at the spending target. Key identifier is the program code (e.g., REB_JPM_VCARD, REB_AMEX_BUS).
lpp.card_rebate_program.grain: One row per card rebate program offered by a bank or card issuer.

lpp.card_settlement_line.description: Represents individual line-item transactions within a card settlement batch, providing transaction-level detail on gross amounts, interchange rates, cross-border flags, and issuer country. Each row corresponds to a single card transaction line settled within a batch, identified by batch_ref (distribution key). This table supports detailed analysis of interchange costs and cross-border activity.
lpp.card_settlement_line.table_type_reason: With 63,237 rows, a batch_ref distribution key, and transaction-level financial measures (gross_amount, interchange_bps), this is clearly a transactional fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.card_settlement_line.grain: One row per individual card transaction line item within a settlement batch.

lpp.cash_balance.description: This table captures point-in-time snapshots of cash balances held across accounts, denominated in various currencies. Each record represents the closing cash balance for a specific account on a specific date in a given currency. Key identifiers include account_ref (distribution key), balance_date (sort/PK), and currency_code (16 distinct ISO currency codes such as AUD, EUR, CHF).
lpp.cash_balance.grain: One row per account, balance date, and currency code combination representing a daily cash position snapshot.

lpp.cash_flow.description: This table records individual cash flow transactions, covering both confirmed actuals and forward-looking forecasts (as indicated by the status field with values CONFIRMED and FORECAST). Each row represents a single cash movement event with its monetary value, currency, transaction date, value/settlement date, and a free-text reference. Key identifiers include account_ref (distribution key) and value_date (sort key), with 16 distinct ISO currencies such as MXN, EUR, JPY.
lpp.cash_flow.table_type_reason: Despite low type confidence and a dimension inference, this table contains transactional measures (flow_amount), event dates, and a status dimension spanning both actuals and forecasts — clearly a fact/event table, not a dimension.
lpp.cash_flow.grain: One row per individual cash flow transaction event identified by account, value date, currency, and reference.

lpp.chargeback.description: This table tracks chargeback disputes raised against card-acquiring transactions, capturing their financial value, classification, reason codes, and lifecycle dates. Each row represents a single chargeback case filed against a specific acquirer, identified by acquirer_ref (distribution key) and initiated_date (sort key). Key attributes include reason_code (card network codes), reason_category, classification (e.g. fraud, processing error), status (e.g. open, won, lost), and both initiated and resolved dates.
lpp.chargeback.table_type_reason: Despite the reference inference, this table has 906 rows of transactional chargeback events with monetary amounts, lifecycle dates, and status — it is a fact table tracking dispute events, not a reference/lookup table.
lpp.chargeback.grain: One row per chargeback dispute case filed against an acquirer transaction.

lpp.company.description: This is a small reference/dimension table (24 rows) containing master data for the legal entities within the organisation. Each row represents a single company entity, uniquely identified by its internal company code (e.g. GR_AE, GR_AU) and its 20-character Legal Entity Identifier (LEI). Key attributes include the company name, country, and structured code following a regional prefix pattern.
lpp.company.grain: One row per legal entity (company), identified by its unique internal company code.

lpp.company_financial_metric.description: This table stores periodic financial metrics and KPIs for companies, covering profitability, leverage, liquidity, and capital structure indicators. Each row represents the financial metrics for a company for a specific reporting period end date and period type (quarterly, full-year, or trailing twelve months). Key measures include revenue, EBITDA, free cash flow, net debt, debt-to-EBITDA ratio, diluted EPS, diluted shares outstanding, and WACC percentage.
lpp.company_financial_metric.table_type_reason: Despite the reference inference, this table contains multiple numeric financial measures (revenue, EBITDA, FCF, net debt, EPS, WACC) reported across time periods — it is a periodic fact table, not a static reference table.
lpp.company_financial_metric.grain: One row per company, reporting period end date, and period type (Q, FY, or TTM).

lpp.counterparty_exposure.description: This table captures periodic snapshots of aggregated financial exposure to counterparties, reported as of a specific date and denominated in a reporting currency. Each row represents the total counterparty exposure measured at a single point in time. Key identifiers include the as_of_date (snapshot date) and reporting_currency.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.table_type_reason: Contains a numeric measure (total_exposure) aggregated at a date grain, making it a periodic snapshot fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.counterparty_exposure.grain: One row per reporting date and reporting currency snapshot of total counterparty exposure.

lpp.credit_rating.description: This table stores credit ratings assigned to entities by major rating agencies (Moody's, S&P, Fitch), including the rating grade, outlook, effective date, and a flag indicating whether the rating is currently active. Each row represents a single credit rating record issued by a specific agency on a given date. Key identifiers include the agency, as_of_date, and rating_grade.
lpp.credit_rating.table_type_reason: Functions as a slowly changing dimension tracking credit rating history per agency and date, with descriptive attributes like grade, outlook, and currency flag.
lpp.credit_rating.grain: One row per credit rating agency and effective date combination representing a point-in-time rating record.

lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.description: This table records individual legs of cross-border payment transactions, capturing the origination and destination countries, payment corridor, FX spread charged in basis points, and lifting fees applied. Each row represents a single leg of a cross-border payment routed through a specific corridor. Key identifiers include the UUID (distribution key) and initiated_at timestamp.
lpp.cross_border_payment_leg.grain: One row per individual cross-border payment leg initiated through a specific origin-to-destination corridor.

lpp.currency.description: This is a reference lookup table listing supported currencies identified by their ISO 4217 3-letter code alongside their full human-readable name. Each row represents a single currency. Key identifier is the currency code (e.g. AED, AUD, USD).
lpp.currency.table_type_reason: Small static lookup table (18 rows) mapping currency codes to descriptions — classic reference data.
lpp.currency.grain: One row per ISO 4217 currency code.

lpp.third_party.description: This table is a directory of third-party entities such as retail partners, customers, and aggregated consumer groups, identified by a unique alphanumeric code and full display name. Each row represents a single third-party entity. Key identifier is the code (e.g. 'TP_CUST_0001', 'RETAIL_CONSUMER').
lpp.third_party.table_type_reason: Acts as a customer/counterparty dimension table used to describe third-party entities across transactions, not a pure static reference table.
lpp.third_party.grain: One row per unique third-party entity identified by its code.

lpp.derivative_mtm.description: This table records the mark-to-market (MTM) valuations of derivative positions, capturing the fair value of each instrument as of a specific valuation date. One row represents a single derivative instrument's MTM valuation on a given date, denominated in a specific currency. Key identifiers include the instrument reference (used as the distribution key) and the valuation date (sort key and primary key).
lpp.derivative_mtm.table_type_reason: Contains quantitative MTM amounts measured at a point in time per instrument per valuation date — this is a periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.derivative_mtm.grain: One row per derivative instrument per valuation date.

lpp.equity_action.description: This table captures corporate actions taken on equity holdings, such as dividend payments, special dividends, and share buybacks. Each row represents a single equity corporate action event on a specific date, including the number of shares involved and the associated monetary amounts. Key fields include action_date, action_type, shares, dividend_per_share, price_per_share, and total_amount.
lpp.equity_action.table_type_reason: Represents discrete business events (corporate actions) with associated measures (shares, amounts, prices) — characteristic of a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.equity_action.grain: One row per equity corporate action event per action date.

lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.description: This table stores linkage records between entities captured as tribal or institutional knowledge within the organization, likely mapping relationships between named entities in an internal knowledge graph. It serves as a bridge or association table connecting disparate entity records. No column metadata is available, but the name suggests it links knowledge graph nodes or business entities.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.table_type_reason: The 'link' suffix and knowledge graph context strongly suggest this is a bridge/association table connecting entity records, not a dimension.
lpp.tribal_knowledge_entity_link.grain: One row per link between two knowledge graph entities.

lpp.fee_rate_card.description: This table defines the negotiated fee rates applicable to various services or transaction types, organized as a rate card with one entry per fee line. Each row represents a specific rate card line item specifying the applicable currency and the contractually agreed fee rate. Key fields include currency_code and negotiated_rate.
lpp.fee_rate_card.table_type_reason: A fee rate card is a static or slowly-changing lookup of contractual rates — it is correctly classified as a reference table.
lpp.fee_rate_card.grain: One row per fee rate card line item per currency.

lpp.forecast_cash_flow.description: This table stores forward-looking cash flow projections organized by forecast snapshot, business category, currency, and projected date. Each row represents a forecasted cash flow amount for a specific flow category (e.g. CAPEX, TAX, AR_COLLECTION) in a given currency for a particular forecast month. Key identifiers include snapshot_id (distribution key), forecast_date (sort key), flow_category, and currency_code.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.table_type_reason: Contains versioned forecast amounts measured across multiple dimensions (date, category, currency, snapshot) — this is a fact table representing forecast lines, not a reference table.
lpp.forecast_cash_flow.grain: One row per forecast snapshot per flow category per currency per forecast date.

lpp.forecast_snapshot.description: Represents a versioned snapshot of a cash forecast, capturing the specific date and cycle type (e.g. monthly 13-week direct or quarterly 18-month indirect) at which a forecast was published. One row corresponds to a single forecast run identified by a unique snapshot ID encoding the date and frequency. Key identifiers include snapshot_id (primary key) and snapshot_date.
lpp.forecast_snapshot.table_type_reason: This is a slowly-changing reference/dimension table of forecast snapshot metadata (38 rows), not a transactional or analytical fact table.
lpp.forecast_snapshot.grain: One row per forecast snapshot (a specific forecast run identified by a unique combination of publication date and forecast cycle type).

lpp.forecast_vs_actual.description: Records the comparison between forecasted and realized cash flow amounts by company, period, and cash flow category (e.g. PAYROLL, CAPEX, AP_DISBURSEMENT, AR_COLLECTION, TAX, FX_REVAL). Each row captures the forecast amount, actual amount, and the resulting variance (absolute and percentage) for a given month-end period. Key identifiers are company_ref, period_date, and flow_category.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.table_type_reason: Contains multiple additive numeric measures (forecast_amount, actual_amount, variance_amount, variance_pct) at a periodic grain — clearly a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.forecast_vs_actual.grain: One row per company, cash flow category, and month-end reporting period.

lpp.fraud_detection_event.description: Captures individual fraud detection events raised against transactions, recording the outcome decision (ALLOW, REVIEW, or BLOCK) made by the fraud detection engine. Each row represents a single fraud evaluation event identified by a UUID and timestamped at the point it was raised. Key identifiers include uuid (distribution key) and raised_at (sort key).
lpp.fraud_detection_event.table_type_reason: Represents discrete transaction-level events (fraud detection decisions) with a timestamp and UUID — characteristic of a fact/event table, not a dimension.
lpp.fraud_detection_event.grain: One row per fraud detection event raised against an individual transaction.

lpp.fraud_loss.description: Records confirmed fraud loss incidents at a granular level, capturing the loss amount, loss date, fraud vector (e.g. card-not-present, social engineering), transaction channel (e.g. ecommerce, in-warehouse), authentication method, and loss category (true fraud vs. friendly fraud). Each row represents a single fraud loss occurrence linked to a company. Key identifiers include company_ref (distribution key) and loss_date (sort key).
lpp.fraud_loss.table_type_reason: Contains additive monetary measures (loss_amount) and descriptive attributes of loss events at a transactional grain — a fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.fraud_loss.grain: One row per individual fraud loss incident recorded against a company on a given date.

lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.description: Stores forecasted foreign exchange exposure positions by company, currency pair, direction (long/short), tenor bucket, and month-end forecast period. Each row quantifies the gross FX exposure amount before hedging for a specific future period and maturity band. Key identifiers include company_ref (distribution key) and forecast_period (sort key).
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.table_type_reason: Contains additive numeric exposure measures (gross_exposure_amount) at a periodic, multi-dimensional grain — characteristic of a fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.fx_exposure_forecast.grain: One row per company, currency, direction, tenor bucket, and month-end forecast period.

lpp.fx_forward.description: Represents individual FX forward deals executed by the organization to hedge or manage foreign currency exposure. Each row captures the lifecycle of a single deal, including its trade date, settlement (value) date, and current status (OPEN, SETTLED, or CANCELLED). The primary identifier is the deal_id (e.g. FXF-0001164).
lpp.fx_forward.table_type_reason: Each row is a discrete transactional FX forward deal event with lifecycle status, trade date, and value date — characteristic of a fact/event table, not a reference table.
lpp.fx_forward.grain: One row per FX forward deal.

lpp.fx_rate.description: Contains daily foreign exchange rates between currency pairs, classified by rate type (SPOT, CLOSING, AVG). Each row represents the exchange rate effective on a specific date for a specific rate type, serving as a lookup for currency conversion across the platform. The composite primary key is (rate_date, rate_type).
lpp.fx_rate.table_type_reason: This is a static lookup/reference table of FX rates used for currency conversion — not a dimension describing a business entity with its own attributes.
lpp.fx_rate.grain: One row per currency pair, rate date, and rate type combination.

lpp.gl_account.description: A reference list of General Ledger (GL) accounts used across the organization, each identified by a structured code combining account number, entity group, country, and account purpose (e.g. '1110-GR_AE_COLLECTION_1'). Each row defines a single GL account with its human-readable description indicating cash type, entity, and purpose. This table serves as the master lookup for GL account codes referenced throughout financial and reconciliation data.
lpp.gl_account.grain: One row per GL account code.

lpp.gl_balance.description: Records month-end General Ledger balances for each GL account, currency, and period combination. Each row captures the monetary balance amount denominated in a specific currency for a given GL account as of a month-end balance date. Key identifiers are gl_account_ref and balance_date, which together form the composite primary key.
lpp.gl_balance.table_type_reason: Each row is a periodic (month-end) snapshot of a measurable balance amount per GL account and currency — characteristic of a periodic snapshot fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.gl_balance.grain: One row per GL account, currency code, and month-end balance date.

lpp.gl_reconciliation.description: Captures month-end reconciliation snapshots comparing GL account balances against an external or bank source, recording the variance amount and reconciliation status (MATCHED or INVESTIGATING). Each row represents the reconciliation result for a specific GL account as of a given month-end date, identified by gl_account_ref and as_of_date. The variance_amount and variance_currency fields quantify any discrepancy between the GL and the reconciling source.
lpp.gl_reconciliation.table_type_reason: Each row is a periodic reconciliation event/snapshot with a measurable variance amount and status outcome — more characteristic of a periodic snapshot fact than a reference table.
lpp.gl_reconciliation.grain: One row per GL account and month-end reconciliation date.

lpp.hedge_relationship.description: This table represents formally designated hedge relationships used to manage foreign exchange or interest rate risk exposures. Each row captures a single hedge relationship with its notional amount, currency, designation date, and lifecycle status (ACTIVE, DEDESIGNATED, or TERMINATED). Key identifiers include the alphanumeric hedge relationship code (e.g. HR-0000684).
lpp.hedge_relationship.table_type_reason: Each row describes a distinct hedge relationship entity with attributes like status and notional amount — it serves as a descriptive/dimensional record rather than a transactional fact or pure reference list.
lpp.hedge_relationship.grain: One row per hedge relationship designation.

lpp.intercompany_transaction.description: This table records financial transactions between entities within the same corporate group, capturing the transfer of funds across legal entities. Each row represents a single intercompany transaction with its monetary amount, currency, transaction and value dates, and processing status (SETTLED or INITIATED). Key identifiers include the unique intercompany reference number (e.g. IC-0006669).
lpp.intercompany_transaction.table_type_reason: Rows represent discrete financial transfer events with amounts, dates, and status — characteristic of a fact/transaction table rather than a reference table.

lpp.interest_accrual.description: This table records daily interest accrual amounts across multiple currencies, capturing how much interest has been earned or owed on a given date. Each row represents the accrued interest amount for a specific accrual date and currency combination. Key fields include accrual_date, amount, and currency_code.
lpp.interest_accrual.table_type_reason: Rows represent periodic financial accrual events with dated monetary amounts, which is characteristic of a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.interest_accrual.grain: One row per interest accrual entry by accrual date and currency.

lpp.investment_instrument.description: This table is a reference catalogue of investable financial instruments available within the treasury investment program, such as money market funds. Each row describes a single investment instrument with its internal code, credit rating, and maturity date. Key identifiers include the internal instrument code (e.g. INV_MMF_0014).

lpp.investment_position.description: This table captures daily snapshots of investment positions held across various instruments and currencies, recording valuation and risk metrics at each reporting date. Each row represents the state of a single investment instrument position as of a specific date, including book value, market value, face amount, duration, and yield to maturity. Key identifiers include the instrument reference and the as-of date.
lpp.investment_position.grain: One row per investment instrument position as of a given valuation date.

lpp.kg_relationship.description: Represents directed relationships between entities in the knowledge graph, capturing how two nodes (entities) are connected by a typed relationship. One row encodes a single edge in the graph, identified by a source entity, a target entity, and a relationship type. This table is a core structural component of the knowledge graph layer.
lpp.kg_relationship.grain: One row per directed relationship between two knowledge graph entities.

lpp.letter_of_credit.description: Represents individual letters of credit (LCs) issued by a bank on behalf of a corporate client, capturing the full lifecycle of each instrument from issuance through expiry or full draw. Each row describes a single LC identified by its unique lc_number, with key attributes including face amount, drawn amount, LC type (e.g. standby, commercial), issue date, expiration date, and current status (OPEN, DRAWN, EXPIRED). This table supports trade finance and working capital management use cases.
lpp.letter_of_credit.grain: One row per letter of credit instrument, identified by lc_number.

lpp.macro_indicator.description: Stores time-series values of macro-economic and financial market indicators used for forecasting, benchmarking, and risk analysis. Each row records the value of a specific indicator (e.g. FED_FUNDS, SOFR_3M, CPI_US, OIL_BRENT, EUR_USD_VOL, GEOPOL_RISK_INDEX) for a given region and date, with the composite primary key of as_of_date, indicator_code, and region ensuring uniqueness. Units and scale vary by indicator (percentage rate, index level, commodity price, etc.).
lpp.macro_indicator.grain: One row per macro-economic indicator, region, and observation date.

lpp.membership_fee.description: Records individual membership fee transactions billed to members, capturing the amount charged, the channel through which the fee was collected (e.g. IN_WAREHOUSE, AUTORENEW, ECOMMERCE), the membership tier (GOLD, EXECUTIVE, BUSINESS), and the payment outcome (COLLECTED, FAILED, REFUNDED, CHARGEBACK). Each row represents a single membership fee billing event tied to a company (company_ref) on a specific issued date. This table supports revenue tracking, renewal analysis, and fee collection performance monitoring.
lpp.membership_fee.table_type_reason: Contains transactional billing events with a measurable fee_amount and payment status outcomes, making it a fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.membership_fee.grain: One row per membership fee billing transaction per member and issued date.

lpp.payment_exception.description: Captures individual payment processing exceptions or errors that were detected and subsequently resolved, recording the type of exception (e.g. duplicate, failed, mismatch), the timestamp it was detected, the timestamp it was resolved, and the number of minutes taken to resolve it. Each row represents a single exception event uniquely identified by a uuid, sorted by detection time. This table supports payments operations, SLA monitoring, and exception management workflows.
lpp.payment_exception.table_type_reason: Represents discrete operational events (exceptions) with timestamps and a resolution duration measure, making it a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.payment_exception.grain: One row per payment exception event, identified by uuid.

lpp.payment_file.description: Represents a payment file batch submitted through the payment processing hub, capturing the transmission lifecycle of grouped payment instructions. Each file contains multiple individual payment transactions bundled together for submission to a clearing rail or bank. Key identifiers include file_uuid (distribution key) and status codes (SENT, RECEIVED, NACK).
lpp.payment_file.table_type_reason: Contains aggregate measures (total_amount, total_count) per file event, making it a fact table tracking payment file submission events rather than a descriptive dimension.
lpp.payment_file.grain: One row per payment file batch submitted through the payment hub.

lpp.payment_hub_throughput.description: Captures daily operational performance metrics for the payment hub, broken down by payment rail (e.g. ACH, WIRE, SEPA_CT, RTP). Each record summarises the volume, value, and straight-through processing (STP) rate for a specific rail on a given date. Key identifiers are metric_date and payment_rail.
lpp.payment_hub_throughput.table_type_reason: Contains time-series numeric measures (volume_count, value_amount, stp_rate_pct) aggregated by date and payment rail — a classic periodic snapshot fact table, not a reference table.
lpp.payment_hub_throughput.grain: One row per payment rail per calendar date.

lpp.transfer.description: Represents individual fund transfer transactions processed through the payment platform, along with rolled-up performance metrics (success rate, repair rate) aggregated by period. Each row captures a transfer's monetary amount, currency, business reference, value date, and processing status (ACK, NACK, REJECTED). Key identifiers include the business reference field and file_uuid (distribution key).
lpp.transfer.table_type_reason: Contains transactional measures (amount, txn_value, txn_count) and event-level status per transfer, consistent with a fact table tracking payment transfer events.
lpp.transfer.grain: One row per individual fund transfer transaction.

lpp.payment_transaction.description: Records individual payment transactions processed through the payment hub, capturing the full lifecycle from initiation to settlement or rejection. Each row represents a single payment transaction identified by its end-to-end ID (E2E), with attributes including amount, currency, execution date, transaction date, status (EXECUTED/REJECTED), and an optional rejection reason code. Key identifier is end_to_end_id.
lpp.payment_transaction.table_type_reason: Stores individual transactional events with measures (amount) and status outcomes per transaction, which is characteristic of a fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.payment_transaction.grain: One row per individual payment transaction identified by its end-to-end reference ID.

lpp.peer_company.description: A small reference table listing competitor and peer companies used for benchmarking analysis, with only 7 rows covering major retail and e-commerce players. Each record identifies a company by its stock ticker code and provides its full legal name, competitive peer group (e.g. BIG_BOX_RETAIL, GROCERY), and market sector classification. The primary key is the ticker code.
lpp.peer_company.grain: One row per peer company identified by its stock ticker symbol.

lpp.peer_company_metric.description: This table stores periodic financial and operational metrics for peer/competitor companies used in benchmarking analysis. Each row captures a snapshot of key performance indicators — such as EBITDA, revenue, free cash flow, debt-to-EBITDA, dividend yield, buyback yield, fraud loss rates, and payments cost ratios — for a peer company at a given reporting period. The primary key is the period date, making it a time-series reference of comparative industry data.
lpp.peer_company_metric.table_type_reason: Contains multiple quantitative measures (EBITDA, revenue, free cash flow, ratios, percentages) across a time dimension, which is characteristic of a fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.peer_company_metric.grain: One row per peer company per reporting period date.

lpp.pension_plan.description: This table is a reference lookup defining the pension plans operated by the organization across different countries. Each row describes a distinct pension plan identified by its country (ISO 2-letter code) and its structural classification (e.g. Defined Benefit or Hybrid). With only 3 rows and diststyle ALL, it is a small, stable reference dataset.
lpp.pension_plan.grain: One row per pension plan, identified by country and plan type.

lpp.pension_valuation.description: This table records actuarial valuations of the company's pension plan(s) as of specific dates. Each row captures the key financial components of a pension valuation — including the projected benefit obligation, plan assets fair value, funded status, discount rate used, and the OCI impact of remeasurements. It serves as a periodic snapshot used for financial reporting and liability management.
lpp.pension_valuation.table_type_reason: Contains multiple financial measures (PBO, plan assets, funded status, OCI impact, discount rate) recorded over time, making it a periodic fact table rather than a static reference.
lpp.pension_valuation.grain: One row per pension valuation as-of date.

lpp.app_user.description: This table is a reference listing of application users and their associated functional roles within the organization. Each row represents a named individual user identified by a unique role/position code (e.g. CFO_GLOBAL, TREAS_HEAD) along with their first name. With only 15 rows, it serves as a small user/persona registry for access control or data personalization purposes.
lpp.app_user.grain: One row per application user, identified by their role code.

lpp.pos_transaction.description: This table records individual point-of-sale (POS) transactions across all sales channels, including in-warehouse, e-commerce, mobile app, kiosk, and membership renewal. Each row represents a single transaction capturing the amount, currency, payment method (card, cash, mobile wallet, gift card, check), sales channel, location code, and exact timestamp. With 80,000 rows distributed by company reference and sorted by transaction timestamp, it is a transactional fact table for payment and sales activity.
lpp.pos_transaction.table_type_reason: Contains transactional measures (amount) with dimensional attributes (channel, payment method, location, currency) and a high row count with a timestamp sort key — clearly a fact table, not a dimension.
lpp.pos_transaction.grain: One row per individual POS transaction.

lpp.sme_feedback_session.description: This table records structured feedback sessions conducted with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), capturing the topic, start time, and end time of each session. It is used to track knowledge-gathering or validation activities as part of a liquidity planning or forecasting process. Key identifiers include the session topic and its temporal bounds (started_at, ended_at).
lpp.sme_feedback_session.table_type_reason: Each row represents a discrete business activity/event (a feedback session) with start and end timestamps, making it a fact/event table rather than a dimension.
lpp.sme_feedback_session.grain: One row per SME feedback session, identified by its topic and start timestamp.

lpp.stress_run_result.description: This table stores the output results of liquidity stress test simulation runs, capturing metrics such as minimum projected cash balance, breach dates, breach severity, and the currency of denomination. Each row represents the outcome of a single stress scenario run, including whether a threshold breach occurred and how severe it was. Key identifiers include the run date (sortkey), breach date, breach severity, and currency code.
lpp.stress_run_result.table_type_reason: Each row captures the quantitative result of a stress simulation run event (min projected cash, breach date, severity), making it a fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.stress_run_result.grain: One row per stress test run result, representing the outcome of a single scenario execution on a given run date.

lpp.stress_scenario.description: This table is a reference catalogue of predefined liquidity stress scenarios used in stress testing, each identified by a unique code and classified by scenario type (e.g., FX_SHOCK, RECEIPTS_DROP, CUSTOMER_DEFAULT). With only 6 rows and ALL distribution style, it serves as a small lookup table describing the assumptions and nature of each scenario. Key identifiers include the scenario code and scenario type.
lpp.stress_scenario.grain: One row per defined stress scenario, identified by its unique scenario code.

lpp.sweep_execution.description: This table records the execution history of cash sweep operations, capturing each sweep event's date, currency, amount transferred, and outcome status (EXECUTED, SKIPPED, or FAILED). It is distributed by instruction reference, linking each execution back to its governing sweep instruction rule. Key identifiers include instruction_ref, execution_date, currency_code, and status.
lpp.sweep_execution.table_type_reason: Each row represents a discrete sweep event/transaction with a monetary amount, date, and status — a classic transactional fact rather than a reference table.
lpp.sweep_execution.grain: One row per sweep execution event, identified by the instruction reference and execution date.

lpp.sweep_instruction.description: This table defines the rules and parameters governing automated cash sweep operations, including the target balance to maintain, the trigger threshold amount, and the currency for each instruction. With only 38 rows and ALL distribution style, it acts as a configuration or dimension table, where each row encodes a unique sweep rule per group, country, and account type. Key identifiers include the instruction code (e.g., SW_GR_AE_OPERATING_1) and target balance currency.
lpp.sweep_instruction.grain: One row per sweep instruction rule, identified by its unique code encoding group, country, account type, and sequence.

lpp.wcf_document.description: Represents individual Working Capital Finance (WCF) documents, such as invoices or payables submitted for financing. Each row captures the lifecycle of a single document including its monetary value, currency, issuance and due dates, and current status (e.g. SUBMITTED, APPROVED, PAID, CANCELLED). Key identifiers include the unique human-readable document_number (e.g. WCF-0000641) and a UUID-based distribution key.
lpp.wcf_document.table_type_reason: Each row represents a transactional business event (a WCF document with an amount, status lifecycle, issue date, and due date), making it a fact table rather than a dimension.
lpp.wcf_document.grain: One row per working capital finance document (e.g. invoice or payable submitted for WCF processing).

lpp.working_capital_metric.description: Stores periodic working capital efficiency metrics calculated at a reporting-period level, including Days Sales Outstanding (DSO), Days Payable Outstanding (DPO), and Days Inventory Outstanding (DIO). Each row captures a snapshot of these key performance indicators for a given period-end date and currency, enabling trend analysis of cash conversion cycle components. The primary key is period_date, suggesting metrics are aggregated to a quarterly or monthly reporting cadence.
lpp.working_capital_metric.table_type_reason: Contains quantitative measures (DSO, DPO, DIO days) aggregated by period, which is characteristic of a periodic snapshot fact table rather than a reference table.
lpp.working_capital_metric.grain: One row per reporting period date (and implicitly currency) for working capital KPI metrics.

1.description: This community centres on knowledge management activities supporting treasury and liquidity planning, specifically the structured capture of Subject Matter Expert (SME) input. The sme_feedback_session table records the topic, timing, and duration of sessions used to gather or validate domain knowledge. It can answer questions about the cadence and coverage of knowledge-gathering efforts, such as which topics have been reviewed and how much time was invested in each.
query_patterns: Which SME feedback sessions have been conducted on a given topic, and when did they take place?
How much total time has been spent in SME feedback sessions within a given date range?
Which topics have had the most recent or the most frequent SME validation sessions?

2.description: This community represents the stress testing reference data layer for liquidity risk management. The stress_scenario table acts as a catalogue of predefined scenarios — such as FX shocks, receipt drops, and customer defaults — each described by a unique code and scenario type. It can answer questions about what stress scenarios are defined, how they are classified, and what assumptions underpin each test.
query_patterns: What liquidity stress scenarios are currently defined, and how are they classified by type?
Which stress scenarios relate to FX shocks versus customer default events?
What are the assumptions and descriptions associated with a specific stress scenario code?

4.description: This community covers the competitive benchmarking reference layer, providing a master list of peer and competitor companies used for comparative analysis. The peer_company table identifies each company by its stock ticker, full legal name, peer group (e.g. BIG_BOX_RETAIL, GROCERY), and market sector. It can answer questions about which companies are included in the benchmarking universe, how they are grouped, and what sector each belongs to.
query_patterns: Which companies are included in the benchmarking peer group, and what sector does each belong to?
Which peer companies are classified under the BIG_BOX_RETAIL competitive group?
What is the full legal name and peer group assignment for a given stock ticker?

5.description: This community holds time-series financial and operational performance data for competitor companies, supporting ongoing benchmarking and competitive intelligence. The peer_company_metric table captures periodic KPI snapshots — including EBITDA, revenue, free cash flow, debt ratios, fraud loss rates, and payments cost ratios — for each peer company. It can answer questions about how competitors perform across key financial metrics over time and how the organisation compares against industry peers.
query_patterns: How has a peer company's EBITDA and free cash flow trended over recent reporting periods?
Which competitor has the lowest fraud loss rate or payments cost ratio in the latest period?
How does the debt-to-EBITDA ratio compare across all peer companies as of the most recent reporting date?

8.description: This is the core cash, liquidity, and banking operations community, integrating bank account master data, daily cash and statement balances, cash flow transactions, GL balances and reconciliations, intercompany transfers, investment positions, sweep instructions and executions, and payment hub throughput metrics. Together these tables provide a comprehensive view of the organisation's cash position, treasury operations, and financial control environment across accounts, currencies, and regions. This cluster can answer questions spanning daily liquidity positioning, cash flow forecasting, GL-to-bank reconciliation, automated sweep performance, and intragroup funding activity.
query_patterns: What is the current cash balance across all bank accounts by region and currency, and how does it compare to the GL balance for the same accounts?
Which cash sweep instructions triggered executions last week, and what was the swept amount and outcome status for each?
What is the net cash flow position (confirmed vs. forecast) for a given account over the next 30 days, broken down by currency?

9.description: This community provides the GL account master reference data that underpins financial reporting and reconciliation processes. The gl_account table defines each General Ledger account with a structured code that encodes account number, entity group, country, and purpose, along with a human-readable description. It can answer questions about the structure of the chart of accounts, the purpose of specific GL codes, and which entities or countries a given account belongs to.
query_patterns: What is the description and purpose of a given GL account code?
Which GL accounts are associated with a specific entity group or country?
How many GL accounts exist per account type or cash purpose across the organisation?

11.description: This community covers the end-to-end payments operations domain, encompassing individual payment transactions, file batches, fund transfers, ACH returns, payment exceptions, fraud detection events, and interest accruals. The frequent joins between transfer, ach_return, and payment_file tables indicate a core focus on tracking payment lifecycle outcomes — from file submission through settlement, rejection, or return. This cluster can answer questions about payment processing performance, failure and return analysis, fraud decision outcomes, exception resolution SLAs, and accrued interest across currencies.
query_patterns: What is the volume and value of ACH returns by reason code over a given period, and which return categories are most prevalent?
How long does it take on average to resolve payment exceptions by exception type, and are SLA targets being met?
What proportion of payment transactions processed through the hub were executed versus rejected, broken down by payment file and transfer rail?

12.description: This community forms the FX, investment, and currency reference data layer for the treasury platform. It combines the currency lookup table with daily FX spot/closing/average rates, forward FX exposure forecasts by tenor and currency pair, and a catalogue of investable instruments such as money market funds. Together these tables can answer questions about currency conversion, hedging coverage relative to gross FX exposure, and the characteristics of instruments available within the treasury investment program.
query_patterns: What is the current spot or closing FX rate for a given currency pair, and how has it moved over the past month?
What is the total forecasted FX exposure by currency pair and tenor bucket for the next quarter, before hedging?
Which investment instruments are available in the treasury program, and what are their credit ratings and maturity dates?

15.description: This community represents the banking relationships, counterparty risk, and market data infrastructure used to manage the organization's external financial exposures. It brings together master data on banks and branches, fee tracking and rate cards, credit ratings, counterparty exposure snapshots, and benchmark interest rates alongside macro-economic indicators. Analysts can use this cluster to monitor banking costs, assess counterparty credit quality, evaluate FX and derivative positions, and benchmark credit facility pricing against prevailing market rates.
query_patterns: What are the total bank fees charged by each banking partner in a given period, and how do they compare to the negotiated rate card?
Which counterparties have the highest aggregated exposure as of the latest snapshot, and what are their current credit ratings from Moody's, S&P, or Fitch?
How have benchmark rates (e.g. SOFR, SONIA) moved over the past quarter, and what is the impact on the floating-rate spread of active credit facilities?

17.description: This community covers corporate financial planning, performance monitoring, and treasury risk management across the organization's legal entities. It integrates cash flow forecasting and variance analysis, capital allocation tracking, company-level financial metrics (leverage, EBITDA, WACC), card rebate programs, fraud loss incidents, and hedge relationships.
