It enables finance teams to answer questions about forecast accuracy, capital deployment against strategic targets, and the financial health of individual entities.
query_patterns: How does the forecasted cash flow for each company compare to actual results by flow category (e.g. CAPEX, PAYROLL) for the latest quarter?
What is the actual capital deployed into each allocation bucket (M&A, Dividends, Debt Paydown) versus the framework target percentage for the current fiscal year?
Which companies have experienced the highest fraud losses by vector or channel, and how does this correlate with their card rebate earnings over the same period?

18.description: This community is a single-table reference cluster providing a standardized lookup of bank service type codes and their descriptions (e.g. account maintenance, wire transfers, ACH credits). It serves as a classification dimension that can be joined to transactional or fee-related tables to label and categorize bank service activity. It supports reporting and filtering of banking operations by service type.
query_patterns: What is the human-readable description for a given bank service type code?
How many distinct bank service types are defined in the reference catalogue?
Which bank service type codes correspond to payment-related services (e.g. wire transfers, ACH)?

19.description: This community contains the AI brain evaluation logging table, which records natural-language query submissions to the organization's AI system along with the generated answer summaries, evaluation timestamps, and graph expansion hop counts. It is designed to support quality assessment and auditability of AI-generated analytical responses. The table is currently empty and serves as infrastructure for future logging and monitoring of AI query performance.
query_patterns: How many AI brain evaluation queries have been submitted and evaluated within a given time window?
What is the average number of knowledge graph expansion hops used across all brain evaluations?
Which queries produced the most recent AI-generated answer summaries, and what were their evaluation timestamps?

20.description: This community covers the working capital and trade finance document lifecycle, anchored by a shared third-party reference directory. It brings together accounts payable invoices from suppliers, accounts receivable invoices issued to customers, working capital finance documents submitted for financing, and the app user registry for access or personalization context. Together these tables support end-to-end visibility into the organization's payables, receivables, and short-term financing activity.
query_patterns: What is the current aging profile of open accounts payable invoices by supplier (third party) and payment terms?
Which accounts receivable invoices are overdue or written off, and which third-party customers do they belong to?
What is the total value of working capital finance documents currently in SUBMITTED or APPROVED status, broken down by currency?

21.description: This community represents the end-to-end card acquiring operations cluster, covering the full lifecycle of card transactions from authorization through settlement and dispute resolution. It includes acquirer reference data, contractual terms, daily SLA performance metrics, individual authorization events, settlement batches, card network classifications, and chargeback cases. Analysts can use this cluster to monitor acquiring costs, track processor performance against SLAs, and analyze fraud-driven chargebacks and dispute outcomes.
query_patterns: Which acquirers are consistently missing their authorization rate or uptime SLA targets, and how does this compare to the contracted SLA thresholds?
What is the total interchange fee and net settlement amount by card network and acquirer for a given month?
What is the chargeback win rate by reason category and acquirer over the past quarter, and what is the total financial value of lost disputes?

23.description: This community focuses on cross-border payment activity, specifically the individual transaction legs that comprise international payment flows. Each record captures the origination and destination countries, the payment corridor, FX spread charged, and any lifting fees applied, enabling analysis of the cost and routing of cross-border payments. It supports treasury and payments teams in monitoring corridor-level pricing, FX cost efficiency, and international payment routing patterns.
query_patterns: What is the average FX spread charged by payment corridor for cross-border transactions in a given period?
Which origination-to-destination country pairs generate the highest volume of cross-border payment legs?
What is the total lifting fee cost incurred across all cross-border payment legs by currency corridor over the past month?

glossary_terms.description: Automated Clearing House — the electronic payment network used for bank-to-bank transfers. In this context, refers to ACH return transactions tracked in the ach_return table.
A rejected or reversed ACH payment sent back by the receiving bank. Captured in the ach_return table with reason codes, categories, amounts, and dates.
NACHA-standard alphanumeric codes (e.g. R01, R02) identifying why an ACH payment was returned. Stored in ach_return.return_reason_code.
NACHA return code for Insufficient Funds — the paying account did not have enough balance to cover the transaction.
NACHA return code for Account Closed — the receiving or originating account has been closed.
NACHA return code for No Account / Unable to Locate — the account number does not correspond to an open account.
NACHA return code for Authorization Revoked — the customer has revoked the authorization for the ACH entry.
NACHA return code for Uncollected Funds — sufficient balance exists but funds are not yet collected/available.
NACHA return code for Customer Advises Unauthorized — the originator did not obtain proper authorization from the customer.
User-facing label for the INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS return category and the R01 return reason code. Indicates the payer lacked sufficient account balance.
User-facing label mapping to the INVALID_ACCT return category in ach_return.return_category. Covers closed or unlocatable accounts.
User-facing label mapping to the UNAUTHORIZED return category in ach_return.return_category. Covers transactions the customer did not authorise.
A high-level classification grouping return reason codes into buckets (INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS, INVALID_ACCT, UNAUTHORIZED, OTHER). Stored in ach_return.return_category.
The date on which an ACH payment was returned by the receiving bank. Stored in ach_return.return_date.
The dollar value of an ACH return transaction. Stored in ach_return.amount.
The acquiring bank or payment processor that processes card or payment transactions on behalf of a merchant. Stored in the acquirer table.
A short identifier or key uniquely referencing an acquirer/processor. Stored in acquirer.code.
Americas — geographic region code used in acquirer.region to identify acquirers operating in North and South America.
Europe, Middle East & Africa — geographic region code used in acquirer.region.
Asia Pacific — geographic region code used in acquirer.region to identify acquirers operating in the Asia-Pacific market.
Latin America — geographic region code used in acquirer.region to identify acquirers operating in Latin American markets.
The lifecycle state of an acquirer contract (e.g. active, expired, terminated). Stored in acquirer_contract.contract_status.
The start date from which an acquirer contract is valid and enforceable. Stored in acquirer_contract.effective_from.
The end or expiry date after which an acquirer contract is no longer valid. Stored in acquirer_contract.effective_to.
Straight-Through Processing — the automated end-to-end processing of a payment transaction without manual intervention. Relevant to ACH and acquirer payment flows.
Month-to-Date — a time period aggregation from the first day of the current month up to today. Commonly used when filtering return amounts or counts.
Year-to-Date — a time period aggregation from the first day of the current year up to today. Used when analysing return trends or acquirer volumes across the year.
Quarter-to-Date — a time period aggregation from the first day of the current quarter up to today. Used for periodic return or contract reporting.
Service Level Agreement — a contractual commitment defining minimum performance thresholds (e.g. uptime, settlement timeliness, auth rates) between an acquirer and a merchant or processor.
Basis Points — a unit equal to 1/100th of a percentage point (0.01%), commonly used to express processor margins, spreads, and fee markups in payment acquiring contracts.

The fee or spread retained by a payment processor/acquirer, expressed in basis points (bps), representing the cost of processing transactions above interchange. Maps to acquirer_contract.processor_margin_bps.
The number of business days between transaction authorisation and actual fund settlement into the merchant's account. Maps to acquirer_contract.settlement_lag_business_days.
The contractually guaranteed percentage of time a payment processing system must remain operational, as defined in an acquirer contract. Maps to acquirer_contract.uptime_sla_pct.
The percentage of payment authorisation attempts that are approved successfully, used as a key acquirer SLA performance metric. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.auth_rate_pct.

The percentage of settlements completed within the contractually agreed settlement lag window, measuring an acquirer's punctuality in funding merchants. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.settlement_on_time_pct.
The actual measured system availability rate for a given period, as recorded in SLA performance reporting. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.uptime_pct.
The date on which an SLA performance metric was recorded or reported. Maps to acquirer_sla_metric.measurement_date.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Euro, used in AP invoice currency fields. Users may refer to it as 'Euro' or 'Euros'.
ISO 4217 currency code for the US Dollar, used in AP invoice currency fields. Users may refer to it as 'US Dollar', 'dollars', or '$'.
ISO 4217 currency code for the British Pound Sterling, used in AP invoice currency fields. Users may refer to it as 'British Pound', 'Sterling', or '£'.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Hong Kong Dollar, used in AP invoice currency fields.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Mexican Peso, used in AP invoice currency fields.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Swedish Krona, used in AP invoice currency fields.
Foreign Exchange currency code — the ISO 4217 three-letter code used to identify a currency in the database (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP). Maps to ap_invoice.currency_code.
The total monetary value of an accounts payable invoice as billed by a vendor. Maps to ap_invoice.invoice_amount.
The date by which an AP invoice must be paid to avoid late payment penalties. Maps to ap_invoice.due_date.
Days Payable Outstanding — a treasury metric measuring the average number of days a company takes to pay its AP invoices, relevant to invoice due dates and payment timing analysis.
Days Sales Outstanding — a treasury metric measuring the average number of days it takes to collect payment after a sale. Relevant to ar_invoice data.
The ratio of invoices paid on or before their due date to total invoices. Directly maps to ap_invoice.on_time_rate. Used to measure AP compliance against payment terms.
Working Capital — a treasury metric representing current assets minus current liabilities. In this context, influenced by outstanding AP (ap_invoice.total_billed vs total_paid) and AR balances.
Payment terms requiring full payment within 30 days of invoice date. Users may say 'Net 30 days' or 'net thirty'; maps to the database code NET_30 in ap_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring full payment within 45 days of invoice date. Users may say 'Net 45 days'; maps to the database code NET_45 in ap_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring full payment within 60 days of invoice date. Users may say 'Net 60 days'; maps to the database code NET_60 in ap_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring full payment within 90 days of invoice date. Users may say 'Net 90 days'; maps to the database code NET_90 in ap_invoice.payment_terms.
Payment terms requiring full payment by end of month plus 5 days. Users may say 'end of month + 5'; maps to the database code EOM_5 in ap_invoice.payment_terms.
Invoice status indicating the invoice has been fully settled. Users may say 'paid', 'cleared', 'settled', or 'closed'; maps to the database value PAID in ap_invoice.status.
Invoice status indicating the invoice is outstanding and awaiting payment. Users may say 'open', 'unpaid', 'outstanding', or 'pending'; maps to the database value OPEN in ap_invoice.status.
Invoice status indicating the invoice has been partially paid. Users may say 'partially paid', 'part paid', or 'underpaid'; maps to the database value PARTIAL in ap_invoice.status.

Invoice status indicating the invoice is under dispute and payment is on hold. Users may say 'disputed', 'contested', 'on hold', or 'in query'; maps to the database value DISPUTED in ap_invoice.status.
The supplier or payee to whom an AP invoice is owed. Users commonly say 'vendor' but the database may use 'supplier' or 'payee'. Relates to entities referenced in ap_invoice.
The buyer or debtor who owes payment on an AR invoice. Users may say 'customer', 'client', or 'buyer'; relates to entities referenced in ar_invoice.
Accounts Payable invoice — a bill received from a vendor that the company owes. Users may refer to it by various names; maps to the ap_invoice table.
Accounts Receivable invoice — a bill issued to a customer that is owed to the company. Users may refer to it by various names; maps to the ar_invoice table.
South Korean Won — the currency code used in ar_invoice.currency_code. Users may say 'Korean won' or 'KRW'; maps to the database value KRW.
Australian Dollar — the currency code used in ar_invoice.currency_code. Users may say 'Australian dollar', 'Aussie dollar', or 'AUD'; maps to the database value AUD.
The date an invoice was issued or created. Maps to ap_invoice.issue_date. Users may also call it billing date, creation date, document date, or raised date.
The date an invoice was paid or settled. Maps to ap_invoice.paid_date. Users may also call it settlement date, cleared date, remittance date, or date paid.
The gross amount charged on an invoice before any payments. Maps to ap_invoice.total_billed. Users may refer to it as billed total, total charges, total invoiced, or gross billed.
The total amount that has been remitted against an invoice. Maps to ap_invoice.total_paid. Users may refer to it as amount paid, paid total, gross paid, or remitted amount.
The month or reporting period to which an invoice belongs. Maps to ap_invoice.year_month. Users may also say 'month', 'invoice month', 'billing month', or 'period'.
The agreed conditions under which a vendor invoice must be paid (e.g. Net 30, Net 60). Maps to ap_invoice.payment_terms. Users may also say 'terms', 'credit terms', 'vendor terms', or 'due terms'.
Accounts Receivable — refers to outstanding invoices owed to the company. Maps directly to the ar_invoice table and its status, amounts, and dates.
Payment terms code meaning payment is due immediately upon invoice receipt. Users may refer to this as 'Due Immediately', 'due on receipt', or 'immediate payment'.
Invoice status code indicating the invoice has been written off as uncollectable. Users may say 'written off', 'bad debt', 'written down', or 'waived'.
Bank statement balance quality status code indicating the balance has passed data validation checks. Users may say 'pass', 'valid', 'clean', 'good data', or 'QA passed'.
Bank statement balance quality status code indicating the balance has failed data validation checks. Users may say 'fail', 'invalid', 'bad data', 'flagged', or 'QA failed'.
ISO currency code for the Japanese Yen. Users may refer to it as 'Japanese Yen', 'yen', or '¥'.
An invoice where ar_invoice.due_date has passed but ar_invoice.status is still OPEN (unpaid). Users may ask about 'past due', 'late invoices', 'delinquent', or 'overdue AR'.
The average number of days between ar_invoice.issue_date and ar_invoice.paid_date for settled invoices. A key AR efficiency metric. Abbreviated as DSO.
The end-of-period bank account balance recorded in bank_statement_balance.amount. Users may call it 'closing balance', 'statement balance', 'end balance', or 'bank balance'.
A unit multiplier equal to 1,000,000. Users may express invoice amounts or bank balances in millions (e.g. '$5 million', '5M', '5mn') which should be converted to the base numeric value.
A unit multiplier equal to 1,000,000,000. Users may express large balances or totals in billions (e.g. '$1 billion', '1B', '1bn') which should be converted to the base numeric value.
A unit equal to 0.01% (one hundredth of a percent). Commonly used in treasury to express interest rate differences or fee rates. 100 bps = 1%.
A unit expressing a proportion out of 100. Used when users ask for rates, shares, or proportions of invoice totals, overdue amounts, or currency breakdowns.
A business entity that owes payment on an invoice. In the AR context, users may say 'customer', 'client', 'buyer', or 'debtor' when referring to the counterparty on ar_invoice records.
A billing document recorded in the ar_invoice table. Users may refer to it as 'bill', 'charge', 'invoice', 'AR record', or 'receivable'.
A financial account whose balances are tracked in bank_statement_balance. Users may say 'bank account', 'account', 'cash account', or 'treasury account'.
Currency — a common treasury abbreviation for currency_code in bank_statement_balance. Users may write 'CCY', 'ccy', or 'currency' when filtering or grouping by currency.

Quality Assurance — refers to the bank_statement_balance.quality_status field. Users may say 'QA status', 'data quality', 'validation flag', or 'check result' when filtering for PASSED or FAILED balances.
Bank Identifier Code — a standard format code used to uniquely identify banks in international transactions. Maps to the bank.bic column in the database.
Legal Entity Identifier — a 20-character ISO 17442 code that uniquely identifies a legal entity participating in financial transactions. Maps to the bank.lei column in the database.

The financial institution or counterparty holding accounts. Users may refer to it as lender, counterparty, or institution — all mapping to the bank table and its descriptive fields (bank.description1, bank.code).
A short internal identifier assigned to a bank record. Maps to bank.code in the database. Users may also call it a bank key, bank ID, institution code, or bank reference.
A unique identifier for a specific bank account record. Maps to bank_account.code in the database. Users may refer to it as account ID, account key, account reference, or account identifier.
An ISO 4217 three-letter code representing the currency denomination of a bank account (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP). Maps to bank_account.currency. Users may also say denomination, FX code, or monetary unit.
The total cash held across one or more bank accounts at a given point in time. Maps to bank_account.total_cash. Users may express this as total balance, cash on hand, account balance, or total funds.
The number of bank accounts associated with a given entity or snapshot. Maps to bank_account.n_accounts. Users may say number of accounts, account total, or account volume.
The date as of which a bank statement balance is reported or valued. Maps to bank_statement_balance.statement_date. Users may call it balance date, report date, as-of date, or valuation date.
The date as of which a bank account rollup or reporting record is captured. Maps to bank_account.rollup_date. Users may also say reporting date, as-of date, balance date, or record date.
Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication — commonly used by users to refer to the BIC routing code that identifies a bank for international wire transfers. Maps to bank.bic.
A point-in-time reference date used in treasury reporting to indicate when a balance or position was recorded. Appears across both bank_statement_balance.statement_date and bank_account.rollup_date.
The maximum monetary amount a signatory is authorised to approve or transact on a bank account, stored in bank_account_signatory.authority_limit_amount.
The date by which a signatory's authorisation must be reviewed and renewed, stored in bank_account_signatory.next_recertify_due_date.
The functional role or permission level assigned to a bank account signatory (e.g. approver, viewer, administrator), stored in bank_account_signatory.role.
The current state of a signatory record indicating whether the signatory is active or inactive on a bank account, stored in bank_account_signatory.status.
A unique identifier for a bank branch, stored in bank_branch.code.

ISO two-letter country code identifying the country of a bank branch, stored in bank_branch.country_code. Common aliases: Australia=AU, United States=US, Mexico=MX, Brazil=BR, Netherlands=NL, Italy=IT.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code AU in bank_branch.country_code.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code US in bank_branch.country_code.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code MX in bank_branch.country_code.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code BR in bank_branch.country_code.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code NL in bank_branch.country_code.
Country alias mapping to the ISO country code IT in bank_branch.country_code.

A geographic grouping of bank branches, stored in bank_branch.region. Common aliases: APAC=Asia-Pacific, AMER=Americas, LATAM=Latin America, EMEA=Europe Middle East Africa, MENA=Middle East North Africa.
Abbreviation for Middle East and North Africa, a geographic region value used in bank_branch.region.
The date on which a bank fee was charged or billed, stored in bank_fee.charge_date.
The monetary value of a bank fee charged to an account, stored in bank_fee.charged_amount.
The currency denomination in which a bank fee is billed, stored in bank_fee.currency_code.
Indicates a bank fee has been marked for review or raised an alert. Maps to the boolean True in the database.
Indicates a bank fee has not been marked for review. Maps to the boolean False in the database.
A short code identifying the type of bank service or fee. Stored in bank_service_type.code.
The human-readable label or description for a bank service type. Stored in bank_service_type.description.
A dimensional rating expressing how reliable or trustworthy a tribal knowledge fact is. Stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.confidence.
A classification dimension that categorises a tribal knowledge entry by its kind or purpose. Stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.fact_type.
Free-text field containing the descriptive content of a tribal knowledge fact. Stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.narrative.
A dimension describing the lifecycle or validity state of a tribal knowledge record. Stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.status.
The timestamp recording when a tribal knowledge fact was logged or entered into the system. Stored in tribal_knowledge_fact.captured_at.
A wire transfer payment method that may appear as a bank service type code or fee description in bank_service_type.
Real-Time Payments — a payment rail that may be referenced as a bank service type code or in tribal knowledge narratives.
The Federal Reserve's instant payment service, potentially referenced in bank service type codes or fee descriptions.
A unit equal to 1/100th of a percentage point (0.01%), commonly used to express fee rates, interest spreads, or confidence thresholds in treasury contexts.
A unit multiplier (1,000,000) used by non-technical users when expressing monetary amounts for bank fees or treasury balances.
A unit multiplier (1,000,000,000) used when expressing large monetary amounts in treasury queries.
A unit expressing a value as a proportion of 100, used for rates, confidence levels, and fee ratios.
Days Inventory Outstanding — a metric measuring average days inventory is held; relevant in working capital knowledge facts.
Weighted Average Cost of Capital — a treasury metric representing blended cost of financing; may be referenced in tribal knowledge facts.
The weighted average interest or fee rate across multiple instruments or services; may appear in knowledge narratives or service descriptions.
Mark-To-Market — the practice of valuing positions at current market prices; may be referenced in tribal knowledge facts related to hedging or investments.
Other Comprehensive Income — an accounting category for unrealised gains/losses; may appear in knowledge facts about hedging or investment portfolios.
The proportion of an exposure that is hedged; a treasury-specific metric that may be described in tribal knowledge narratives.
Annual Recurring Revenue — a revenue metric sometimes referenced in treasury knowledge facts for forecasting or liquidity planning.
Loan-To-Value — a ratio used in lending and treasury contexts to assess collateral coverage; may appear in knowledge facts.

variants: Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation Amortisation
glossary_terms.description: Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortisation — a profitability metric that may be referenced in treasury knowledge narratives for covenant or liquidity analysis.
Euro Short-Term Rate — the overnight benchmark interest rate for the Euro, published by the ECB. Used as a floating rate index on credit facilities and benchmark rate tables.
Secured Overnight Financing Rate — the USD overnight benchmark rate administered by the New York Fed, replacing LIBOR for US Dollar instruments.
Sterling Overnight Index Average — the GBP overnight benchmark rate administered by the Bank of England, replacing GBP LIBOR.
Tokyo Overnight Average Rate — the JPY overnight benchmark rate administered by the Bank of Japan.
Mexican Interbank Equilibrium Rate (28-Day) — the MXN short-term benchmark rate published by Banco de México.
Swiss Average Rate Overnight — the CHF overnight benchmark rate administered by SIX, replacing CHF LIBOR.
Euro Interbank Offered Rate (3-Month) — the 3-month EUR term benchmark rate published by the European Money Markets Institute.
Australian Bank Bill Swap Rate (3-Month) — the 3-month AUD benchmark rate administered by ASX.
3-Month US Treasury Bill rate — a short-term USD government benchmark rate often used as a risk-free reference.
HKD Overnight Index Average — the Hong Kong Dollar overnight benchmark rate.
Certificado de Depósito Interbancário — the BRL overnight interbank benchmark rate widely used in Brazilian financial markets.
Singapore Overnight Rate Average — the SGD overnight benchmark rate administered by the Monetary Authority of Singapore.
Canadian Dollar Offered Rate — the CAD short-term benchmark rate based on bankers' acceptance rates.
Overnight tenor — the shortest standard rate term, referring to a one-business-day maturity for benchmark rates.
1-Month tenor — a benchmark rate term with a one-calendar-month maturity.
3-Month tenor — a benchmark rate term with a three-calendar-month maturity.
Swiss Franc — the official currency of Switzerland, identified by ISO 4217 code CHF in the database.
Brazilian Real — the official currency of Brazil, identified by ISO 4217 code BRL in the database.
Singapore Dollar — the official currency of Singapore, identified by ISO 4217 code SGD in the database.
Canadian Dollar — the official currency of Canada, identified by ISO 4217 code CAD in the database.

The published reference interest rate (e.g. SOFR, ESTR, SONIA) used as the floating rate basis for credit facilities and derivative instruments. Stored in the benchmark_rate table as the 'rate' column.
The date on which a benchmark rate is officially published or observed. Maps to benchmark_rate.rate_date in the database.
The total size of a credit facility — the maximum amount a lender has committed to make available to a borrower. Maps to credit_facility.commitment_amount.
The unique identifier for a credit facility in the database. Users may refer to it as a deal code, credit line ID, or facility reference. Maps to credit_facility.code.
The benchmark rate linked to a credit facility's interest calculation. Users may call it the base rate, reference rate, or rate index. Maps to credit_facility.benchmark_code.
The title or heading of a tribal knowledge fact entry. Users may call it a name, label, subject, or heading. Maps to tribal_knowledge_fact.title.
The condition or context under which a tribal knowledge fact should be applied. Maps to tribal_knowledge_fact.trigger_condition.
A committed borrowing arrangement between a lender and a borrower. Users may refer to it as a credit line, loan facility, revolving credit, or deal.
The credit spread or margin charged over a benchmark rate, expressed in basis points. Maps to credit_facility.spread_bps.
The total effective interest rate on a borrowing, inclusive of spread and base rate. Maps to borrowing.all_in_rate.
The face value or notional amount drawn under a borrowing. Maps to borrowing.principal_amount.
The date on which a borrowing or credit facility is due to be repaid or expires. Maps to borrowing.repayment_date and credit_facility.maturity_date.
The date on which funds are disbursed or drawn under a borrowing. Maps to borrowing.drawdown_date.
The date on which a credit facility becomes active or is signed. Maps to credit_facility.start_date.
The current lifecycle state of a credit facility or borrowing (e.g. active, expired). Maps to credit_facility.status and borrowing.status.
ISO currency code for the Polish Zloty. Users may say 'Polish Zloty' or 'zloty'; the database stores 'PLN' in borrowing.currency_code.
Borrowing status indicating the loan has not yet been repaid. Users may say 'outstanding', 'active', or 'open'; the database stores 'OUTSTANDING' in borrowing.status.
Borrowing status indicating the loan has been fully repaid. Users may say 'repaid', 'closed', or 'settled'; the database stores 'REPAID' in borrowing.status.
Foreign Exchange — used by users to refer to the currency or denomination of a borrowing. Related to borrowing.currency_code.
An individual drawdown or loan made under a credit facility, with its own principal, rate, and repayment terms. Corresponds to the borrowing table.
The effective all-in interest rate representing the total cost of a borrowing to the entity. Maps to borrowing.all_in_rate.
The proportion of a credit facility that has been drawn down via borrowings, expressed as a percentage of total facility size.
Capital Expenditures — funds deployed for long-term asset investments. Maps to the CAPEX code in the capital_allocation_actual.bucket column.
Mergers & Acquisitions — capital allocated toward acquisition activity. Maps to the M_AND_A code in the capital_allocation_actual.bucket column.
Dividend payments to shareholders — a capital allocation bucket representing cash returned to equity holders. Maps to the DIVIDENDS code in capital_allocation_actual.bucket.
Debt Paydown — capital allocated to repaying outstanding debt obligations. Maps to the DEBT_PAYDOWN code in capital_allocation_actual.bucket.
Share Buybacks — capital deployed to repurchase the company's own shares. Maps to the BUYBACKS code in capital_allocation_actual.bucket.
3D Secure — an authentication protocol used in card transactions to verify the cardholder. Represented in card_authorization.auth_3ds_status.
Monetary value of a transaction or capital allocation, expressed in currency units. Used across card_authorization.amount and capital_allocation_actual.amount.
The planned or strategic percentage weight assigned to a capital allocation bucket under the treasury framework. Stored in capital_allocation_actual.framework_target_pct.
The as-of or period-end date for a capital allocation record, typically aligned to a quarter or fiscal period end. Stored in capital_allocation_actual.period_date.
The date and time at which a brain evaluation was run or assessed. Stored in brain_evaluation.evaluated_at.
The number of traversal steps or query expansion iterations performed during a brain evaluation. Stored in brain_evaluation.expansion_hops.
The original natural-language input question submitted for evaluation. Stored in brain_evaluation.query_text.
The free-text output or response generated by a brain evaluation run. Stored in brain_evaluation.answer_summary.
A classification category for how capital is allocated or deployed (e.g. CAPEX, M&A, Dividends). Stored as a code in capital_allocation_actual.bucket.
A card authorization event representing a requested charge or payment approval. Corresponds to records in the card_authorization table.
Card Not Present — indicates a transaction where the physical card was not used at a terminal (e.g. online or phone purchases). Maps to cnp_indicator = true in the database.
The elapsed time in milliseconds between an authorization request and the response from the issuer. Maps to response_time_ms. Also referred to as processing time or round trip time.
User-facing term for a successful authorization outcome. Maps to decision = 'APPROVED' in the database.
User-facing term for a rejected authorization outcome. Maps to decision = 'DECLINED' in the database.
User-facing term for an authorization that did not receive a response within the allowed window. Maps to decision = 'TIMEOUT' in the database.
User-facing term for an authorization that failed due to a system or processing error. Maps to decision = 'ERROR' in the database.
A code returned by the issuer explaining why an authorization was declined. Maps to decline_reason_code in the database.
A three-letter code (e.g. USD, EUR, GBP) identifying the currency of a transaction per ISO 4217 standards. Maps to currency_code in the database.
A categorical band grouping transactions by their monetary value (e.g. small, medium, large). Maps to transaction_size_band in the database.
The total monetary value of settled transactions before fees or deductions are applied. Maps to gross_sales in card_settlement_batch.
The number of individual transactions included in a settlement batch. Maps to batch_count in card_settlement_batch.
The date and time at which an authorization request was initiated. Maps to auth_request_ts in card_authorization.
The date and time at which an authorization decision was returned. Maps to auth_response_ts in card_authorization.

The fee paid to the card-issuing bank for processing a card transaction, deducted from gross sales during settlement. Maps to card_settlement_batch.interchange and card_settlement_batch.interchange_amount.

The final amount deposited to the merchant after all fees (interchange, network assessment, processor margin) are deducted from gross sales. Maps to card_settlement_batch.net_settlement and card_settlement_batch.net_settlement_amount.
The fee charged by the card brand/network (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) for use of their payment scheme, separate from interchange. Maps to card_settlement_batch.network_assess.
The date on which transaction data is aggregated and summarised into a settlement batch. Maps to card_settlement_batch.rollup_date.
The exact date and time at which settled funds were credited to the merchant's bank account. Maps to card_settlement_batch.bank_deposit_ts.
The date and time at which a card settlement batch was finalised and closed for processing. Maps to card_settlement_batch.batch_close_ts.
The total value of card transactions before any fee deductions, representing the full charged amount. Maps to card_settlement_batch.gross_sales_amount.

The business entity that accepts card payments and receives net settlement funds. Users may refer to this as 'merchant' while the database context refers to the payout recipient in settlement batch records.
The card scheme or brand (e.g. Visa, Mastercard, Amex) that facilitates card transactions and charges network assessment fees. Users may refer to this as the card brand, scheme, or association.
A grouped collection of card transactions processed together for settlement, corresponding to a record in card_settlement_batch. Users may call this a batch, settlement file, or daily settlement.
The fee charged by the card network (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) to the acquirer/processor per settlement batch. Stored in card_settlement_batch.network_assessment_amount.
The revenue or markup retained by the payment processor on top of interchange and network fees. Stored in card_settlement_batch.processor_margin_amount.
The date and time at which the processor completed funding/settlement for a batch. Stored in card_settlement_batch.processor_settle_ts.
The portion of card spend that qualifies for rebate calculation under the rebate programme terms. Stored in card_rebate_earning.eligible_spend.
The rebate dollar amount earned by the organisation for a given period based on eligible card spend. Stored in card_rebate_earning.rebate_earned.
The end date of the rebate earning period used for reporting and rebate accrual. Stored in card_rebate_earning.period_date.
The Visa card network. Referenced in the database as code = 'VISA' in card_network.code.
The Mastercard card network. Referenced in the database as code = 'MASTERCARD' in card_network.code.
The American Express card network. Referenced in the database as code = 'AMEX' in card_network.code.
The Discover card network. Referenced in the database as code = 'DISCOVER' in card_network.code.
The Costco co-branded / private label card network. Referenced in the database as code = 'COSTCO_PRIVATE' in card_network.code.
The UnionPay card network, primarily used in China. Referenced in the database as code = 'UNIONPAY' in card_network.code.
A credit card network type where spend is billed to the cardholder on a deferred basis. Stored as network_type = 'CREDIT' in card_network.
A charge card network type where the full balance is due at end of period (no revolving credit). Stored as network_type = 'CHARGE' in card_network.
A private label card network type — a closed-loop card accepted only at a specific retailer or brand. Stored as network_type = 'PRIVATE_LABEL' in card_network.
A PIN-authenticated debit card network type. Stored as network_type = 'DEBIT_PIN' in card_network.
The short code identifier for a card network in the database (e.g. VISA, MASTERCARD, AMEX). Stored in card_network.code.
The human-readable name of a card network (e.g. 'Visa', 'Mastercard'). Stored in card_network.name.
The category of a card product (Credit, Charge, Private Label, Debit PIN). Stored in card_network.network_type.
An alternative term users use to refer to a card network (e.g. Visa scheme, Mastercard scheme). Maps to card_network in the database.
A user-facing term for rebate earned on card spend programmes. Maps to card_rebate_earning.rebate_earned in the database.
Basis points — a unit equal to 1/100th of a percentage point (0.01%), used to express rebate rates and interchange fees in this treasury context.
The rebate rate expressed in basis points earned on card spend, mapped to card_rebate_program.rebate_bps_at_target. Represents the earn rate at the program target.
The interchange fee rate in basis points charged by the card network per transaction, mapped to card_settlement_line.interchange_bps.
The classification of a card transaction by purchase type or merchant category, mapped to card_rebate_earning.spend_category.
The unique identifier for a card rebate program, mapped to card_rebate_program.code.
The classification or category of a card rebate program, mapped to card_rebate_program.program_type.
Alias for cross-border transactions where card_settlement_line.cross_border = true. Users say 'international' or 'foreign' to mean cross-border.
Alias for non-cross-border transactions where card_settlement_line.cross_border = false. Users say 'domestic' to mean not international.
The total pre-fee transaction value for a card settlement, mapped to card_settlement_line.gross_amount.
The date as of which a cash balance is recorded or reported, mapped to cash_balance.balance_date.
The country of the bank that issued the card used in a settlement transaction, mapped to card_settlement_line.issuer_country.
The aggregated cash balance across accounts at a given date, mapped to cash_balance.amount aggregated over relevant accounts.
Percentage — used by users to express rates or shares; must be converted to basis points (×100) or decimals when querying bps columns.
Earnings Per Share — the portion of a company's profit allocated to each outstanding share. Maps to company_financial_metric.diluted_eps (diluted basis).
A leverage ratio measuring how many years of EBITDA would be required to repay total debt. Stored in company_financial_metric.debt_to_ebitda.
Earnings per share calculated including all dilutive securities (options, warrants, convertibles). Stored in company_financial_metric.diluted_eps.
The current stage or outcome of a chargeback case. Users may refer to this as case status, dispute status, chargeback state, resolution status, or case stage. Maps to chargeback.status.

A high-level grouping of chargeback dispute reasons (e.g. fraud, processing error). Users may call this dispute reason group, reason group, dispute basis, or dispute classification. Maps to chargeback.reason_category.

The specific card-network-assigned code identifying the basis for a chargeback. Users may call this dispute code, chargeback code, card network code, or reason identifier. Maps to chargeback.reason_code.
The date a chargeback case was closed or settled. Users may refer to this as close date, settlement date, resolution date, decision date, or case close date. Maps to chargeback.resolved_date.
A short alphanumeric identifier for a legal entity or business unit. Users may call this entity code, firm code, organization code, or company ID. Maps to company.code.
The full registered or trading name of a company. Users may refer to this as firm name, entity name, organization name, or business name. Maps to company.name.
The domicile or geographic location of a company. Users may refer to this as nation, geography, location, or domicile. Maps to company.country.
Free Cash Flow. Maps to company_financial_metric.free_cash_flow. Represents cash generated after operating expenses and capital expenditures.
Trailing Twelve Months. A period_type value stored as 'TTM' in company_financial_metric.period_type. Represents a rolling 12-month lookback window for annualised metrics.
Full Year. A period_type value stored as 'FY' in company_financial_metric.period_type. Represents an annual reporting period.
Quarterly. A period_type value stored as 'Q' in company_financial_metric.period_type. Represents a three-month fiscal reporting period.
Total financial debt minus cash and cash equivalents. Maps to company_financial_metric.net_debt. Used to assess a company's true leverage position net of available liquidity.
Total income generated from business operations (top line). Maps to company_financial_metric.revenue. Can be referenced by users as sales or top-line figures.
Total share count including the dilutive effect of options, warrants, and convertible securities. Maps to company_financial_metric.diluted_shares_outstanding.

Classification of the financial reporting window. Maps to company_financial_metric.period_type. Users may say 'quarterly', 'annual', or 'trailing twelve months' which must resolve to DB codes Q, FY, or TTM respectively.
The currency in which counterparty exposure values are expressed. Maps to counterparty_exposure.reporting_currency. Users may say 'currency', 'base currency', or 'functional currency'.

The markup or differential between the mid-market exchange rate and the rate applied to a cross-border payment, expressed in basis points. Stored as fx_spread_bps in the cross_border_payment_leg table.
The total financial risk amount owed to or by a counterparty, representing the gross credit or market risk. Stored as total_exposure in the counterparty_exposure table.
A standardised score or grade assigned by a ratings agency reflecting the creditworthiness of a counterparty. Stored as rating_grade in the credit_rating table.
Moody's Investors Service — a major credit rating agency. Users refer to it as 'Moody's' but the database stores it as 'MOODYS' in the credit_rating.agency column.
Standard & Poor's — a major credit rating agency. Users refer to it as 'S&P' or 'Standard & Poor's' but the database stores it as 'SP' in the credit_rating.agency column.
Fitch Ratings — a major credit rating agency. Users refer to it as 'Fitch' and the database stores it as 'FITCH' in the credit_rating.agency column.
An organisation that assigns credit ratings to counterparties or instruments. Stored in the credit_rating.agency column. Known aliases include Moody's (MOODYS), S&P (SP), and Fitch (FITCH).
A flag indicating whether a credit rating is the most recent/active rating for a counterparty, as opposed to a historical rating. Stored as is_current (true/false) in the credit_rating table.
The directional indicator accompanying a credit rating, reflecting expected near-term trajectory. Stored as outlook in the credit_rating table with values: STABLE, POSITIVE, NEGATIVE, WATCH.
A rating outlook indicating no expected near-term change in credit rating. Users say 'Stable' and the database stores it as 'STABLE' in the credit_rating.outlook column.
A rating outlook indicating a potential downgrade in the near term. Users say 'Negative' and the database stores it as 'NEGATIVE' in the credit_rating.outlook column.
A rating outlook indicating a potential upgrade in the near term. Users say 'Positive' and the database stores it as 'POSITIVE' in the credit_rating.outlook column.
A rating outlook status indicating the counterparty is under active review for a potential rating change. Users say 'Watch' and the database stores it as 'WATCH' in the credit_rating.outlook column.
The directional route of a cross-border payment between two regions or countries. Stored as corridor in cross_border_payment_leg with codes such as US-EU, US-APAC, EU-APAC, US-MX, US-CA.
A cross-border payment corridor from the United States to Europe. Users say 'US to Europe' but the database stores it as 'US-EU' in the cross_border_payment_leg.corridor column.
A cross-border payment corridor from the United States to the Asia-Pacific region. Users say 'US to Asia-Pacific' but the database stores it as 'US-APAC'.
A cross-border payment corridor from Europe to the Asia-Pacific region. Users say 'Europe to Asia-Pacific' but the database stores it as 'EU-APAC'.
A cross-border payment corridor from the United States to Mexico. Users say 'US to Mexico' but the database stores it as 'US-MX' in the cross_border_payment_leg.corridor column.
A cross-border payment corridor from the United States to Canada. Users say 'US to Canada' but the database stores it as 'US-CA' in the cross_border_payment_leg.corridor column.
The receiving or beneficiary country for a cross-border payment leg, stored as ISO country codes (e.g. MX, GB, JP, DE, CA) in the cross_border_payment_leg.destination_country column.
The fee charged for processing or transferring a cross-border payment, covering wire or transaction charges. Stored as lifting_fees in the cross_border_payment_leg table.

The other party in a financial transaction or credit arrangement. In this system, 'counterparty' maps to entities tracked in the counterparty_exposure table, and may also be referred to as a bank, institution, or trading partner.
The country from which a cross-border payment originates. Users may refer to this as the sending, source, remitting, or payer country. Maps to cross_border_payment_leg.origination_country.
The full descriptive name of a currency (e.g. 'US Dollar', 'Euro'). Maps to currency.description in the database.

An external counterparty, customer, or partner entity recorded in the system. Users may refer to these as customers, partners, companies, or organizations. Maps to third_party.code and third_party.name.
The unique identifier code for a third-party entity. Maps to third_party.code in the database.
The display name of a third-party entity. Maps to third_party.name in the database.
The date on which a derivative's mark-to-market value is calculated or recorded. Maps to derivative_mtm.valuation_date in the database.
The currency in which the mark-to-market value of a derivative is expressed or reported. Maps to derivative_mtm.mtm_currency in the database.
The date on which an equity corporate action (such as a dividend or buyback) takes effect or is recorded. Maps to equity_action.action_date in the database.
A classified event affecting an equity instrument, such as a dividend payment, special dividend, or share buyback. Maps to equity_action.action_type in the database.
A standard cash dividend corporate action event. Stored as the code 'DIVIDEND' in equity_action.action_type.
A one-off or non-recurring dividend corporate action event. Stored as the code 'SPECIAL_DIVIDEND' in equity_action.action_type.
A share repurchase corporate action event where a company buys back its own stock. Stored as the code 'BUYBACK' in equity_action.action_type.
The current market-based valuation of a derivative instrument, equivalent to its mark-to-market amount. Maps to derivative_mtm.mtm_amount in the database.
A payment transaction that crosses national borders, tracked at the leg level including origination country. Maps to the cross_border_payment_leg table.
Dividend Per Share — the monetary amount distributed to shareholders for each share held, stored in equity_action.dividend_per_share.
Dividend Per Share as a treasury metric used to evaluate equity actions and shareholder distributions recorded in equity_action.dividend_per_share.
The price paid or received per share in an equity action (e.g. buyback), mapped to equity_action.price_per_share.
The number of shares involved in an equity action, mapped to equity_action.shares.
The gross monetary value of an equity transaction, mapped to equity_action.total_amount.
The agreed fee rate on a rate card, typically expressed as a ratio or percentage, mapped to fee_rate_card.negotiated_rate.
Tax Payment — a cash flow category for scheduled tax disbursements, mapped to flow_category value 'TAX' in forecast_cash_flow.
Accounts Receivable Collection — a cash inflow category representing collections from customers, mapped to flow_category value 'AR_COLLECTION' in forecast_cash_flow.
Intercompany Transfer — a cash flow category for fund movements between legal entities within the same group, mapped to flow_category value 'INTERCOMPANY' in forecast_cash_flow.
Debt Service — a cash flow category covering principal repayments and interest payments on borrowings, mapped to flow_category value 'DEBT_SERVICE' in forecast_cash_flow.
Accounts Payable Disbursement — a cash outflow category for payments made to vendors/suppliers, mapped to flow_category value 'AP_DISBURSEMENT' in forecast_cash_flow.
Payroll — a cash outflow category for employee salary and wage payments, mapped to flow_category value 'PAYROLL' in forecast_cash_flow.
The projected monetary value of an expected cash flow for a given date and category, mapped to forecast_cash_flow.forecast_amount.
The date or period for which a cash flow projection is made, mapped to forecast_cash_flow.forecast_date.
A classification of a treasury cash movement (e.g. CAPEX, PAYROLL, DEBT_SERVICE), mapped to forecast_cash_flow.flow_category.

A short-term cash flow forecast covering a 13-week (rolling quarter) horizon, produced on a monthly cycle using the direct method (i.e., based on actual cash receipts and disbursements). Stored in forecast_snapshot.description.

A medium-to-long-term cash flow forecast covering an 18-month horizon, produced on a quarterly cycle using the indirect method (i.e., derived from projected P&L and balance sheet movements). Stored in forecast_snapshot.description.

FX Revaluation — non-cash accounting adjustments to the value of foreign currency-denominated assets and liabilities due to exchange rate movements. Users may refer to this as 'FX reval' or 'currency revaluation'. Stored in forecast_vs_actual.flow_category.

The difference between the forecasted amount and the actual amount for a given period and flow category. A positive variance indicates an under-spend vs forecast; negative indicates over-spend. Captured in forecast_vs_actual.variance_amount and forecast_vs_actual.variance_pct.
The variance expressed as a percentage of the forecast amount, indicating relative forecast accuracy. Stored in forecast_vs_actual.variance_pct.
The realised cash flow amounts recorded for a given period, as opposed to planned or forecasted figures. Stored in forecast_vs_actual.actual_amount.
A unique identifier for a specific forecast snapshot run or version. Used to join or filter forecast data. Stored in forecast_snapshot.snapshot_id.
A descriptive label categorising a forecast by its methodology and horizon (e.g., direct vs indirect, 13-week vs 18-month). Stored in forecast_snapshot.description.

A cash flow forecasting methodology that projects cash flows based on expected cash receipts and disbursements directly (as opposed to adjusting net income). Referenced in the 'Monthly 13-week direct forecast' description.

A cash flow forecasting methodology that derives projected cash flows by adjusting net income for non-cash items and working capital changes. Referenced in the 'Quarterly 18-month indirect forecast' description.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction is permitted to proceed without restriction.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction requires manual review before processing.
Fraud detection decision code indicating a transaction has been declined or blocked due to suspected fraud.
Authentication method code where the cardholder was actively challenged (e.g. via OTP or biometric) during the 3-D Secure flow.
Authentication method code where 3-D Secure authentication completed without an active user challenge (frictionless flow).
Authentication method code indicating the transaction did not use 3-D Secure authentication.
Authentication method code indicating no authentication was applied to the transaction.
Sales channel code representing online/digital transactions conducted through a web or mobile storefront.
Sales channel code representing in-person transactions completed at a physical warehouse or store location.
Sales channel code representing transactions associated with the renewal of a customer membership subscription.
Fraud vector code representing fraud where the physical card is not used at the point of sale, typically in online or phone transactions.
Fraud vector code representing fraud where victims are psychologically manipulated into authorising payments or revealing credentials.
Loss category code for disputes where a legitimate cardholder falsely claims a transaction was unauthorised, resulting in a chargeback.
Loss category code for genuine fraud losses where a transaction was carried out by an unauthorised third party.
FX exposure direction code indicating a long position, meaning the entity holds more of a currency than it needs (net buyer).
FX exposure direction code indicating a short position, meaning the entity owes more of a currency than it holds (net seller).
The monetary value of confirmed fraud losses recorded in the fraud_loss table, representing the financial impact of fraudulent transactions.
The total unhedged or raw foreign currency exposure before netting or hedging instruments are applied, as recorded in fx_exposure_forecast.
A reversal of a transaction initiated by the card issuer on behalf of the cardholder; maps to fraud loss records with a loss_category of FRIENDLY_FRAUD or TRUE_FRAUD.
User-facing term for the fraud_detection_event.decision field — the outcome assigned to a transaction by the fraud rules engine.
User-facing term for fraud_loss.auth_method — describes how a transaction was authenticated at the time of the fraud event.
User-facing term for fraud_loss.channel — the originating commerce channel through which a fraudulent transaction occurred.
User-facing term for fraud_loss.fraud_vector — the method or mechanism by which fraud was perpetrated.
User-facing term for fraud_loss.loss_category — the high-level categorisation of a fraud loss as either Friendly Fraud or True Fraud.
User-facing term for fx_exposure_forecast.forecast_period — the date or month to which a foreign currency exposure forecast applies.
User-facing term for fx_exposure_forecast.direction — whether the treasury position is long (surplus) or short (deficit) in a given currency.
A contractual agreement to buy or sell a currency at a predetermined rate on a future settlement date. Stored in the fx_forward table.
The exchange rate between two currencies at a given point in time. Stored in the fx_rate table as the rate column.
The current market exchange rate for immediate currency settlement. Maps to rate_type = SPOT in the fx_rate table.
The exchange rate recorded at the end of the business day. Maps to rate_type = CLOSING in the fx_rate table.
The arithmetic mean exchange rate over a defined period. Maps to rate_type = AVG in the fx_rate table.
A time-band grouping of FX exposures or forward contracts by their remaining duration until maturity. Stored in fx_exposure_forecast as tenor_bucket.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or forwards maturing within 0 to 1 month. Maps to tenor_bucket = '0-1M'.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or forwards maturing between 1 and 3 months. Maps to tenor_bucket = '1-3M'.
Tenor bucket representing exposures or forwards maturing between 3 and 6 months. Maps to tenor_bucket = '3-6M'.
A unique identifier for an FX forward transaction. Users may refer to this as deal number, trade ID, or contract ID. Maps to fx_forward.deal_id.
The date on which an FX forward deal was executed or booked. Maps to fx_forward.trade_date.
The future date on which an FX forward contract is due for settlement or delivery. Maps to fx_forward.value_date.
The current lifecycle state of an FX forward contract. Maps to fx_forward.status with values OPEN, SETTLED, or CANCELLED.
An FX forward deal that has been booked but not yet settled or cancelled. Maps to fx_forward.status = 'OPEN'.
An FX forward deal that has been fully delivered and completed. Maps to fx_forward.status = 'SETTLED'.
An FX forward deal that was voided or terminated before settlement. Maps to fx_forward.status = 'CANCELLED'.
The date on which an FX rate is effective or was recorded. Maps to fx_rate.rate_date.
A General Ledger account used to record financial transactions. Stored in the gl_account table with a code and description.
The alphanumeric identifier for a General Ledger account. Maps to gl_account.code.
The human-readable label or description for a General Ledger account. Maps to gl_account.description.
The face value or principal amount of an FX forward contract in the base or terms currency, used to measure exposure size.
General Ledger — the master record of all financial transactions. Maps directly to the gl_balance and gl_reconciliation tables, and the gl_account_ref identifier column.

Reconciliation status in gl_reconciliation.status indicating the GL account balance has been fully reconciled with no outstanding variance. Users may say 'matched', 'clean', 'reconciled', or 'in balance'.
Reconciliation status in gl_reconciliation.status indicating an unresolved variance is under review. Users may say 'open', 'unreconciled', 'in progress', 'break', or 'exception'.
Maps to gl_balance.amount — the carrying value of an account as recorded in the general ledger. Users may say 'ledger balance', 'GL amount', 'account balance', or 'balance'.
Maps to the hedge_relationship table, identified by hedge_relationship.code. Users may refer to it as 'hedge', 'hedge ID', 'hedge program', 'hedging relationship', or 'hedge reference'.
Intercompany: shorthand for transactions between entities within the same corporate group, corresponding to the intercompany_transaction table. Often seen in reference numbers and reporting labels.
A hedge relationship with status = ACTIVE in the database. Users may refer to live, open, current, or in-force hedges to mean the same thing.
A hedge relationship with status = TERMINATED in the database. Users may say closed, unwound, cancelled, or ended hedge.
A hedge relationship with status = DEDESIGNATED in the database. Occurs when a hedge no longer qualifies for hedge accounting. Users may say de-designated, failed hedge, or broken hedge.
An intercompany_transaction with status = SETTLED. Users may refer to completed, paid, cleared, or finalised transactions.
An intercompany_transaction with status = INITIATED. Users may refer to pending, open, in-flight, in-progress, or outstanding transactions.
The currency of the Eurozone. Maps to the database code EUR in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of the United States. Maps to the database code USD in intercompany_transaction.currency_code.
The currency of the United Kingdom. Maps to the database code GBP in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Japan. Maps to the database code JPY in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Mexico. Maps to the database code MXN in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Canada. Maps to the database code CAD in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Australia. Maps to the database code AUD in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Brazil. Maps to the database code BRL in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of China. Maps to the database code CNY in hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Hong Kong. Maps to the database code HKD in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of South Korea. Maps to the database code KRW in both intercompany_transaction.currency_code and hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Singapore. Maps to the database code SGD in hedge_relationship.notional_currency.
The currency of Sweden. Maps to the database code SEK in intercompany_transaction.currency_code.
The currency of Poland. Maps to the database code PLN in intercompany_transaction.currency_code.
The currency of the United Arab Emirates. Maps to the database code AED in intercompany_transaction.currency_code.
A unit multiplier equal to 1,000. Users may express smaller transaction or notional amounts as '500K' or '500 thousand', which should be interpreted as 500,000 in database queries.
The date on which a hedge relationship was formally designated for hedge accounting, stored in hedge_relationship.designation_date. Marks the inception of the hedge.
The date on which an intercompany transaction was booked or initiated, stored in intercompany_transaction.transaction_date.
The unique identifier for an intercompany transaction, stored in intercompany_transaction.reference. Used to look up or audit individual payments.
Highest short-term credit rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may describe instruments with this rating as 'highest short-term rated' or 'top-tier short-term'.
High short-term credit rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may refer to instruments as 'high short-term rated' rather than using the code.
Highest long-term money market fund rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may refer to it as 'money market AAA' or 'top-rated money market'.
Highest long-term credit rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may refer to instruments as 'triple-A rated' or 'highest rated'.
Very high quality long-term credit rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may describe this as 'double-A plus' or 'very high quality'.
High quality long-term credit rating stored in investment_instrument.rating. Users may describe instruments as 'double-A rated' or 'high quality'.
Interest rate sensitivity of an investment position measured in days, stored as investment_position.duration_days. Indicates how sensitive a position's value is to interest rate changes.
The interest earned but not yet paid or received, stored as interest_accrual.amount. Represents the cumulative interest accruing on an investment instrument over time.
The date on which interest is accrued or posted, stored as interest_accrual.accrual_date. Used to filter accrual records by time period.
The snapshot or reporting date for an investment position, stored as investment_position.as_of_date. Indicates the date on which the position's values (book value, duration) were recorded.
The unique identifier for an investment instrument, stored as investment_instrument.code. Users may refer to this by various names rather than the column name.
Yield to Maturity: the total annualised return anticipated on a bond if held until maturity, stored as a percentage in investment_position.yield_to_maturity.
Letter of Credit: a bank-issued financial instrument guaranteeing payment; the primary entity in the letter_of_credit table, referenced by users as 'LC' across all related fields.
The nominal or stated principal value of a financial instrument. Applies to investment positions (investment_position.face_amount) and letters of credit (letter_of_credit.face_amount).
The current market price of an investment position, reflecting real-time or period-end valuations; stored in investment_position.market_value.
Annualised return of a bond or fixed-income instrument if held to maturity, expressed as a percentage in investment_position.yield_to_maturity.
The portion of a letter of credit that has been drawn down or utilised by the beneficiary; stored in letter_of_credit.drawn_amount.
The date on which a letter of credit ceases to be valid; stored in letter_of_credit.expiration_date. Users frequently call this 'maturity date' or 'expiry date'.
The date on which a letter of credit was formally issued or became effective; stored in letter_of_credit.issue_date.
The unique identifier for a letter of credit record; stored in letter_of_credit.lc_number. Users may refer to it as 'LC ID', 'LC code', or 'credit number'.
The classification or category of a letter of credit (e.g. standby, commercial, revolving); stored in letter_of_credit.lc_type.
LC status alias: when users say 'Drawn' or 'called', the database stores the code 'DRAWN' in letter_of_credit.status.
LC status alias: when users say 'Expired', 'matured', or 'lapsed', the database stores the code 'EXPIRED' in letter_of_credit.status.
The stated nominal or principal value of a bond or investment instrument at issuance, as opposed to its current market value; maps to investment_position.face_amount.
Federal Funds Rate — the overnight interest rate at which US banks lend reserves to each other, set by the Federal Reserve. Used as a key macro indicator in treasury rate benchmarking.
3-Month SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate) — a 3-month tenor benchmark interest rate based on overnight US Treasury repo transactions, replacing LIBOR as the standard floating rate reference.
Geopolitical Risk Index — a macro indicator measuring the level of global geopolitical uncertainty and risk, used in treasury scenario analysis and FX/commodity hedging decisions.
US Consumer Price Index — a macro indicator tracking the average change in prices paid by US consumers for goods and services, used in treasury inflation risk assessment.
EUR/USD Volatility — a macro indicator measuring the implied or realised volatility of the Euro to US Dollar exchange rate, used in FX risk management and hedging strategies.
Brent Crude Oil Price — the benchmark price for North Sea crude oil, used as a global oil price reference in treasury commodity exposure and hedging analysis.
United States — the geographic region code used in the macro_indicator table to scope indicator readings to the US market.
Global / Worldwide — the geographic region code used in the macro_indicator table to scope indicator readings to worldwide or cross-regional coverage.
Auto Renewal channel — membership fees collected via automatic recurring billing, typically through a stored payment method.
Mail Renewal channel — membership fees collected via mailed invoices or paper-based renewal notices.
New Signup channel — membership fees associated with first-time member enrollment or new account origination.
Gold membership tier — a standard membership level in the membership fee structure.
Executive membership tier — a premium membership level, typically above Gold, in the membership fee structure.
Business membership tier — a membership level tailored for business or commercial members in the membership fee structure.
Collected / Paid status — indicates a membership fee that has been successfully received and settled.
Chargeback / Disputed status — indicates a membership fee that has been disputed by the member and reversed by the payment network.
Refunded status — indicates a membership fee that was previously collected but subsequently returned to the member.

Hedge Ratio — a treasury metric expressing the proportion of an exposure that is covered by a hedging instrument. Informed by macro indicators such as EUR_USD_VOL and OIL_BRENT to size FX or commodity hedges.

Blended Rate — a weighted average interest rate across multiple instruments or tranches. In this context, derived from macro indicators such as FED_FUNDS and SOFR_3M to represent an overall funding or investment rate.
Wire Transfer — a high-value electronic payment rail. Stored as the value 'WIRE' in payment_hub_throughput.payment_rail.
SEPA Credit Transfer — the Single Euro Payments Area credit transfer rail used across Europe. Stored as the value 'SEPA_CT' in payment_hub_throughput.payment_rail.
Payment file status indicating the file has been transmitted/sent. Stored as the value 'SENT' in payment_file.status.
Payment file status indicating the file has been received and acknowledged. Stored as the value 'RECEIVED' in payment_file.status.
Negative Acknowledgement — a payment file status indicating the file was rejected by the receiving party. Stored as the value 'NACK' in payment_file.status.
The percentage of payments that flow through end-to-end without manual intervention. Maps to payment_hub_throughput.stp_rate_pct.
The time taken to resolve a payment exception, expressed in minutes. Maps to payment_exception.resolution_time_minutes.
The clearing channel or network used to process a payment (e.g. WIRE, ACH, RTP, SEPA_CT). Maps to payment_hub_throughput.payment_rail.
The category or classification of a payment exception or failure. Maps to payment_exception.exception_type.
The processing or delivery state of a payment file. Maps to payment_file.status.
The total monetary value of all payments in a payment file or batch. Maps to payment_file.total_amount.
The number of individual payment transactions within a payment file or batch. Maps to payment_file.total_count.
The currency in which a payment file or batch is denominated and settled. Maps to payment_file.total_currency.
The timestamp when a payment exception was closed or resolved. Maps to payment_exception.resolved_at.
UAE Dirham. A valid value in payment_file.total_currency.
Chilean Peso. A valid value in payment_file.total_currency.
Unit of time used to measure exception resolution duration. Maps to payment_exception.resolution_time_minutes.
The proportion of transfers that complete successfully, mapped to transfer.success_rate. Expressed as a ratio.
The proportion of transfers that required manual correction or repair before settlement, mapped to transfer.repair_rate.
The number of individual payment transactions processed, mapped to transfer.txn_count or payment_hub_throughput.volume_count.
The total monetary value of payment transactions, mapped to transfer.txn_value or transfer.amount or payment_hub_throughput.value_amount.
The date dimension used for aggregating or summarising transfer activity, mapped to transfer.rollup_date.
ISO 4217 currency code for the Chinese Yuan Renminbi. Users may say 'yuan', 'renminbi', or 'RMB'; the database stores 'CNY' in transfer.currency_code.
A unique identifier assigned to each payment transfer, mapped to transfer.reference. Used to look up or trace individual transactions.
The total monetary value of payments processed through the payment hub, mapped to payment_hub_throughput.value_amount.

0.description: Returns the aggregated total cash balance summed across all bank accounts as of the most recent completed statement date (yesterday).
cte_steps: latest_snapshot: filter BalanceSnapshot to rows where statement_date equals yesterday's date
total_balance: sum the amount across all accounts from latest_snapshot
required_aggregations: Sum of balance amount across all bank accounts
required_filters: statement_date = yesterday

1.description: Returns the daily closing balance for the JPMorgan operating account for each of the last 7 calendar days.
cte_steps: jpmorgan_account: identify the BankAccount record(s) associated with JPMorgan as the banking institution
recent_balances: filter BalanceSnapshot to the identified account(s) where statement_date falls within the last 7 days, ordered by date
required_aggregations: Closing balance amount per day
required_filters: Bank name matches JPMorgan
Account purpose is operating
statement_date within last 7 days

2.description: Lists all individual wire transfer payment transactions with an amount exceeding $1 million that were processed on today's date.
cte_steps: todays_wires: filter PaymentTransaction to rows where transaction_date equals today, payment rail is WIRE, and amount exceeds 1,000,000
wire_details: return all relevant attributes of the filtered wire transactions
required_aggregations: Count of qualifying wire transactions
List of individual wire amounts
required_filters: payment rail = WIRE
transaction_date = today

3.description: Lists all bank accounts that have recorded a negative balance at any point during the current week.
cte_steps: current_week_snapshots: filter BalanceSnapshot to rows where statement_date falls within the current calendar week
negative_balances: filter current_week_snapshots to rows where amount is less than zero
account_details: join negative_balances to BankAccount to enrich with account name, currency, and region
required_aggregations: Minimum balance per account during the week
Count of days with negative balance per account
required_filters: statement_date within current week
balance amount < 0

4.description: Returns the total sum of ACH credit/receipt transactions processed on the previous day.
cte_steps: ach_receipts_yesterday: filter PaymentHubThroughput (or Transaction) to rows where payment_rail is ACH, the direction is inbound/credit, and metric_date equals yesterday
total_receipts: sum the value amount across all qualifying ACH receipt rows
required_aggregations: Sum of ACH receipt value amounts for yesterday
required_filters: payment_rail = ACH
transaction direction is inbound/receipt
date = yesterday

5.description: Returns a grouped list of all bank accounts organized by their currency denomination, showing counts and account identifiers per currency.
cte_steps: account_currency_map: select all BankAccount records with their currency_code and account identifiers
grouped_by_currency: group accounts by currency_code and aggregate count of accounts per currency
required_aggregations: Count of bank accounts per currency

6.description: Returns the total count of open bank accounts where the account's country is Canada.
cte_steps: canada_accounts: filter BankAccount (joined to BankBranch or country attribute) to rows where country equals Canada (CA)
account_count: count the number of qualifying Canadian bank accounts
required_aggregations: Count of bank accounts in Canada
required_filters: country = CA (Canada)

7.description: Returns a full daily cash position report showing account balances and net cash flows across all entities as of last Friday.
cte_steps: last_friday_date: derive the calendar date of the most recent Friday
balances_on_friday: filter BalanceSnapshot to rows where statement_date equals last Friday
flows_on_friday: filter Transaction to rows where value_date equals last Friday and aggregate net inflows and outflows
cash_position_report: join balances and flows to BankAccount and Company to produce the full position by entity and account
required_aggregations: Sum of opening/closing balances per account
Sum of inflows and outflows per account on that date
required_filters: statement_date = last Friday
value_date = last Friday

8.description: Returns the most recent FX rate for the USD/CAD currency pair stored in the system, filtered to the SPOT or CLOSING rate type.
cte_steps: usd_cad_rate: filter FxRate to rows where the currency pair is USD/CAD and select the latest available rate_date
current_rate: return the rate value and rate_type (SPOT or CLOSING) for the identified record
required_aggregations: Latest rate value for USD/CAD pair
required_filters: currency pair = USD/CAD
rate_date = most recent available date

9.description: Compares actual cash inflows against forecasted amounts by legal entity over the past 30 days, highlighting entities where the variance exceeds 10%.
cte_steps: date_range: define the 30-day lookback window ending on the most recent available date
actual_inflows: aggregate actual cash inflow amounts from ForecastActual (or Transaction) by company and period within the date range
forecast_inflows: aggregate forecasted inflow amounts from ForecastLine or ForecastActual by company and period within the date range
variance_calc: join actuals and forecasts by company and period, compute absolute and percentage variance
flagged_entities: filter variance_calc to rows where absolute percentage variance exceeds 10%, and join to Company for entity names
required_aggregations: Sum of actual inflow amounts per entity per period
Sum of forecast inflow amounts per entity per period
Absolute variance (actual minus forecast)
Percentage variance relative to forecast
required_filters: flow direction is inbound/inflow
period_date within last 30 days
percentage variance > 10%

30.description: Lists all debt drawdowns with outstanding repayment status whose repayment date falls within the next 90 days, showing principal amount, currency, facility, and days to maturity.
cte_steps: upcoming_maturities: filter DebtMaturity to rows where status is OUTSTANDING and repayment_date is within the next 90 days from today
facility_detail: join to Bond to enrich each maturity with facility name, currency, and benchmark
required_aggregations: Sum of principal_amount by facility
Count of maturing tranches
required_filters: status = OUTSTANDING
repayment_date between today and today + 90 days

31.description: Returns all open letters of credit with their LC number, issuing bank, face amount, drawn amount, currency, and expiration date.
cte_steps: open_lcs: filter LetterOfCredit to rows where status is OPEN
lc_summary: select lc_number, issuing bank reference, face_amount, drawn_amount, currency, expiration_date and compute days until expiry
required_aggregations: Total face_amount of open LCs
Total drawn_amount of open LCs
required_filters: status = OPEN

32.description: Calculates available borrowing capacity for revolving credit facilities by subtracting total outstanding principal from the committed facility limit.
cte_steps: revolving_facilities: filter Bond to rows classified as revolving credit facilities (e.g. facility code contains RCF) with ACTIVE status
outstanding_drawdowns: aggregate DebtMaturity by facility_ref, summing principal_amount where status is OUTSTANDING
available_capacity: join revolving facilities to outstanding drawdowns and compute commitment_amount minus total outstanding principal as available capacity
required_aggregations: Sum of principal_amount per facility where status is OUTSTANDING
Commitment_amount minus total outstanding principal to derive available capacity
required_filters: Bond facility type is revolving (RCF)
Bond status is ACTIVE
DebtMaturity status = OUTSTANDING

33.description: Shows the net cash position grouped by geographic region for the current week, derived from balance snapshots and transaction flows across all accounts.
cte_steps: current_week_balances: filter BalanceSnapshot to statement_dates within the current week
latest_balance_per_account: for each account_ref, select the most recent balance snapshot within the week
account_region_map: join BankAccount to BankBranch to resolve each account to its geographic region
net_cash_by_region: aggregate latest balance amounts by region
required_aggregations: Sum of balance amount per region using the most recent snapshot per account within the current week
required_filters: statement_date within the current calendar week

34.description: Returns the total notional amount of all active (ACTIVE) FX hedge positions, optionally broken down by currency and hedge type.
cte_steps: active_hedges: filter HedgePosition to rows where status is ACTIVE
total_notional: aggregate notional_amount across all active hedges, grouped by currency_code
required_aggregations: Sum of notional_amount across all ACTIVE hedge positions
Sum of notional_amount grouped by currency_code
required_filters: status = ACTIVE

35.description: Lists all investment positions whose instruments mature within the next 30 days, showing instrument reference, face amount, book value, yield, and maturity date.
cte_steps: maturing_instruments: filter InvestmentInstrument to rows where maturity_date is within the next 30 days from today
position_detail: join InvestmentPosition to maturing instruments to retrieve face_amount, book_value, market_value, and yield_to_maturity for the latest as_of_date
required_aggregations: Sum of face_amount for maturing positions
Sum of book_value for maturing positions
required_filters: InvestmentInstrument maturity_date between today and today + 30 days

36.description: Shows the covenant compliance status for all active credit facilities, comparing current financial metrics against policy thresholds to identify any breaches or at-risk covenants.
cte_steps: active_facilities: filter Bond to rows with ACTIVE status to get facility limits and covenant terms
outstanding_debt: aggregate DebtMaturity by facility_ref summing principal_amount where status is OUTSTANDING
latest_financials: filter CompanyFinancialMetric to the most recent reporting period to retrieve leverage and liquidity metrics
compliance_check: join facilities, debt balances, and financials then compare utilisation and debt_to_ebitda against facility covenant thresholds and flag breaches
required_aggregations: Sum of outstanding principal per facility
Facility utilisation as outstanding principal divided by commitment_amount
Debt-to-EBITDA ratio from CompanyFinancialMetric
required_filters: Bond status = ACTIVE
DebtMaturity status = OUTSTANDING
